Appendix E: If your team uses Kotlin#

Appendices · Chapter 59· 9 min read· Quick reference

Kotlin is a second language for the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Kotlin code calls Java code, and Java code calls Kotlin code. Spring Boot supports Kotlin fully. The syntax of Kotlin is much closer to C# than the syntax of Java is. But the platform under Kotlin is exactly the Java platform in this book.

KindC#JavaNote
twistpublic record Customer(string Name, int Age)data class Customer(val name: String, val age: Int)This is Kotlin, not Java. A data class is like a record, and its properties are real properties. Why
twistann with { Age = 41 }ann.copy(age = 41)In Kotlin, copy with a named argument does the same as a with expression in C#. Java has no with expression. Why
twiststring? name = found?.Nameval name: String? = found?.nameC# only warns about an unchecked use of a nullable value, but Kotlin refuses to compile it Why
trapexpecting a different runtimethe same JVM, Spring and JPAKotlin changes the syntax only, so type erasure, proxies and virtual threads work as in Java Why
twistclass OrderController(OrderService service)class OrderController(private val service: OrderService)in Kotlin, the class header is the constructor, and Spring injects through that constructor Why
trapa class Spring can subclassa Kotlin class, final unless marked openwithout the kotlin-spring plugin, start-up fails with "Cannot subclass final class" Why
trapan entity class, written in Kotlina Kotlin @Entity classin Kotlin, the kotlin-jpa plugin adds the no-argument constructor but leaves the entity final Why
trapstring name = directory.FindName(2)val name: String = directory.findName(2)Kotlin does not check a value from Java, so this compiles and throws if Java returns null Why
twiststatic members and optional parameters@JvmStatic and @JvmOverloadsKotlin code needs these annotations to look natural when Java code calls it Why
twistasync Task<Report> and awaitsuspend fun and async { ... }.await()Kotlin coroutines look like async and await, and suspend spreads to every caller too Why
twistchoosing a language for a teamKotlin or JavaKotlin needs less extra code, and its compiler checks nulls. Far more developers know Java. Why

What Kotlin gives back that Java took awaynew#

Imagine your first day on a Kotlin team. Many C# features that you missed in Java are back. Each C# feature in this table has a direct Kotlin form. For the same feature, Java has a workaround or nothing:

C# featureJavaKotlin
PropertiesgetX() / setX()val / var, real properties
Nullable reference typesOptional plus annotationsString? in the type system
Extension methodsstatic utility classesextension functions
String interpolationnone"$name has ${x.size}"
Operator overloadingnoneoperator fun plus
Recordsrecorddata class
with expressionnonecopy()
Named and optional argumentsnonefull support
Top-level functionsnone, everything in a classsupported
switch expressionswitch expressionwhen expression
async/awaitvirtual threadscoroutines, plus virtual threads

Here is one small piece of code in C# and in Kotlin. It has a customer type with a computed label, a changed copy, and a search that may find nothing:

C#
public record Customer(string Name, int Age)
{
    public string Label => $"{Name} ({Age})";
}

var ann = new Customer("Ann", 40);
var older = ann with { Age = 41 };
var customers = new List<Customer> { ann, older };
Customer? found = customers.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Name == "Bob");
string? name = found?.Name;
Kotlin
data class Customer(val name: String, val age: Int) {
    val label get() = "$name ($age)"
}

val ann = Customer("Ann", 40)
val older = ann.copy(age = 41)
val customers = listOf(ann, older)
val found: Customer? = customers.firstOrNull { it.name == "Bob" }
val name: String? = found?.name
Reading the code
data class Customer(val name: String, val age: Int) {

This line declares a data class. A data class in Kotlin is like a record. The compiler writes equals, hashCode and toString from the properties in the header. It also writes copy. val makes each property read-only. Each type comes after the name of its property.

val label get() = "$name ($age)"

This is a computed property, like a C# property written with =>. $name puts a value into the string, as {Name} does in C#.

val older = ann.copy(age = 41)

copy with a named argument does the same as with in C#. Kotlin has no new keyword, so Customer("Ann", 40) creates the object.

val found: Customer? = customers.firstOrNull { it.name == "Bob" }

Customer? is a type that may be null. The braces are a lambda, and it is the one parameter of the lambda.

val name: String? = found?.name

This is the same safe call as ?. in C#. There is no Bob, so name is null here. When you use such a value without a check, C# only warns. Kotlin refuses to compile the code.

Gotcha

The side-by-side panes in this book show C# and Java. On a Kotlin project the right-hand side changes, but the runtime facts do not change. Type erasure, the equality contract and the traps of Jakarta Persistence (JPA) are unchanged. Annotations that work through proxies are unchanged too. Virtual threads, the class loader, the tuning of garbage collection (GC) and the whole of Spring are also unchanged. Kotlin is a different front end to the same platform.

Kotlin with Spring Bootnew#

Spring supports Kotlin fully. It does not only tolerate Kotlin. Spring Boot 4 needs Kotlin 2.2 or later. Here is the shop's order controller written in Kotlin. The code assumes two things. An OrderService has a find method that returns an OrderDto?, which is null when there is no such order. An OrderNotFound exception exists, and the application turns it into a 404 response:

import jakarta.validation.Valid
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/orders")
class OrderController(private val service: OrderService) {

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    fun get(@PathVariable id: Long): OrderDto =
        service.find(id) ?: throw OrderNotFound(id)

    @PostMapping
    fun create(@RequestBody @Valid command: CreateOrder): OrderDto =
        service.create(command)
}
Reading the code
class OrderController(private val service: OrderService) {

The constructor is written in the class header. private val also keeps the parameter as a private property. So this one line is both the field and the constructor. Spring injects through this constructor with no annotation. Spring does the same for a Java class that has only one constructor.

fun get(@PathVariable id: Long): OrderDto =

fun declares a function, and the return type comes after the parameters. The = introduces a body that is a single expression, like => in C#.

service.find(id) ?: throw OrderNotFound(id)

?: is called the Elvis operator. It uses the right-hand side when the left-hand side is null, like ?? in C#. In Kotlin, throw is an expression, so it can be on the right-hand side, as it can in C#.

fun create(@RequestBody @Valid command: CreateOrder): OrderDto =

The annotations are the same as in Java. Each annotation is written before its parameter.

A few Kotlin rules change how Spring behaves, and the build needs two compiler plugins:

ConcernWhat to know
Constructor injectionconstructor parameters in the class header, and no annotation is needed
Final by defaultKotlin classes and functions are final unless marked open, which breaks CGLIB proxies
kotlin-spring pluginIt opens classes that have Spring annotations, and their functions. This plugin is essential.
kotlin-jpa pluginIt generates the no-argument constructor that JPA needs on entities, but leaves them final. Hibernate also needs them open, for lazy loading.
Null safety across the boundarySpring 7's JSpecify annotations tell Kotlin which values may be null
Coroutines in controllerssuspend functions work in both Spring MVC and WebFlux controllers
Gotcha

Without the kotlin-spring compiler plugin, @Transactional and every other proxy-based annotation fails, in one of two ways. Here is the first way. A Kotlin class is final unless it is marked open, and Code Generation Library (CGLIB) proxies work by subclassing. So start-up fails with Cannot subclass final class.

The second way is worse. If someone writes open on the class but not on its functions, start-up succeeds. Each final function is left out of the proxy, so its annotation does nothing. The function also runs on the proxy object itself, and the injected fields of the proxy object are null. The only sign at start-up is a warning that the method “cannot get proxied via CGLIB”.

The same failure is described in the chapter How Spring actually works. Here the failure has a different cause. On any Kotlin Spring project where an annotation seems to be ignored, check the plugin first.

Calling Java from Kotlin and backtrap#

The null checks of Kotlin stop at the edge of Kotlin code. Suppose the shop still has a Java class, CustomerDirectory. Its findName method returns the name of a customer, or null when there is no such customer. There is no customer 2:

PredictA Java method that returns null, called from Kotlin#
Both declarations compile. What does each one do when it runs?
val directory = CustomerDirectory()

val maybe: String? = directory.findName(2)
println(maybe?.length ?: 0)

val name: String = directory.findName(2)
Show the answer
The first prints 0. The second throws NullPointerException: findName(...) must not be null.

Kotlin's null safety does not cover platform types. Kotlin cannot know whether a value from Java may be null. So Kotlin trusts the type that you choose, and does not force a check. When such a value is used as a non-null type, Kotlin adds a check that throws on that same line. A NullPointerException in Kotlin code almost always comes from a value that crossed the boundary from Java code.

Declare a value from Java as nullable, as maybe is. Spring Framework 7 helps here. Its signatures now have JSpecify annotations, and Kotlin reads them. A Java method marked @Nullable cannot be assigned to a non-null Kotlin type at all, because the compiler reports a type mismatch.

Java code sees Kotlin code through a few conventions:

DirectionWhat happens
Kotlin calls JavaJava types arrive as "platform types". Kotlin does not know whether they can be null, and does not check.
Java calls KotlinA data class is an ordinary class to Java. Each val becomes a getX() method, and each var adds setX().
Kotlin null safety at the boundarya Java method returning null into a non-null Kotlin val throws at the assignment
Default arguments from Javanot visible unless the function is annotated @JvmOverloads
Top-level functions from Javaappear as static methods on a class named after the file, such as FileNameKt
Companion object membersneed @JvmStatic to look static from Java

Coroutines against virtual threads#

The Kotlin way of waiting for the network is older than virtual threads. It looks much like the C# way. Suppose a report needs a customer from one service and the orders of that customer from another service. The code fetches both at the same time. customerClient and orderClient are clients for those two services, and their calls are asynchronous:

C#
async Task<Report> BuildReportAsync(long customerId)
{
    Task<Customer> customer = customerClient.FindAsync(customerId);
    Task<List<Order>> orders = orderClient.FindByCustomerAsync(customerId);
    return new Report(await customer, await orders);
}
Kotlin
import kotlinx.coroutines.async
import kotlinx.coroutines.coroutineScope

suspend fun buildReport(customerId: Long): Report = coroutineScope {
    val customer = async { customerClient.find(customerId) }
    val orders = async { orderClient.findByCustomer(customerId) }
    Report(customer.await(), orders.await())
}
Reading the code
suspend fun buildReport(customerId: Long): Report = coroutineScope {

suspend marks a function that can pause without blocking its thread, as async does in C#. coroutineScope waits for everything that was started inside it. This is structured concurrency.

val customer = async { customerClient.find(customerId) }

async starts the call and returns at once with a Deferred. A Deferred in Kotlin does the same as a Task in C#. Both calls now run at the same time.

Report(customer.await(), orders.await())

await waits for each result. If one call fails, the scope cancels the other call. C# needs a CancellationToken to do that.

C#KotlinJava 21+
async Task<T>suspend funa plain blocking method
awaitjust call the suspend functionjust call the method
Task.WhenAllawaitAll / coroutineScopeStructuredTaskScope, still preview
CancellationTokenthe coroutine Job hierarchythread interrupt, or a scope
Function colouringyes, because suspend spreads to every callerno
Note

With coroutines, the problem that virtual threads removed is back. Once a function is suspend, every function that calls it must be suspend too. In exactly the same way, async spreads through C# code. In exchange, coroutines give you structured concurrency that has been stable for years. StructuredTaskScope in Java is still a preview. On a Kotlin project, follow the choice that the team has already made, instead of mixing coroutines and virtual threads.

Should you argue for Kotlin?#

Reason to choose itReason to stay on Java
Genuinely less ceremony, particularly for data and null handlingThe Java talent pool is far larger
Null safety enforced by the compilerRecords, patterns and virtual threads closed much of the gap
Excellent Spring and Gradle supportOne language means one set of build and tooling problems
Your team already knows itKotlin adds a compiler plugin dependency to Spring

Here is an honest summary for someone who comes from C#. Kotlin will feel comfortable sooner, and Java has removed much of the difference since version 8. Kotlin is not a wrong choice, and Java is not a wrong choice. On an existing codebase, the choice is rarely yours to make.

Check yourself
1
A Kotlin build for Spring Boot needs two compiler plugins, kotlin-spring and kotlin-jpa. What does each one do?
kotlin-spring opens every class that has a Spring annotation, and the functions of that class. Spring can then wrap the class in a proxy. Without the plugin, a Kotlin class is final. kotlin-jpa generates the no-argument constructor that JPA needs on an entity. It leaves the entity final. Hibernate also needs the entity to be open, for lazy loading.

Quick reference#

KotlinWhat it meansC#Java
val x = 1a read-only variable or propertyreadonly, or { get; }final
var x = 1a variable or property you can changea field, or { get; set; }a field that is not final
String?a type that may be null, checked by the compilerstring?, with warnings only@Nullable, checked by tools
a?.bnull if a is nulla?.bOptional.map
a ?: bb when a is nulla ?? bObjects.requireNonNullElse(a, b)
a!!a, or a NullPointerException if it is nulla!, which does not checkObjects.requireNonNull(a)
"$name, ${a.b}"a string template$"{name}, {a.b}"concatenation, or formatted()
data classa class with equals, hashCode, toString and copy generatedrecordrecord
c.copy(age = 41)a copy with one property changedc with { Age = 41 }no equivalent
fun f(x: Int = 0)a default argumentan optional parameterone overload per case
when (x) { ... }a switch expressionswitch expressionswitch expression
object Registrya single instance, created on first usea static classan enum with one constant, or static members
companion objectmembers that belong to the class, not to an instancestatic membersstatic members
suspend funa function that can pause without blockingasync Taska plain method, run on a virtual thread
@JvmStatic, @JvmOverloadsmake Kotlin code look natural when called from Java--
Next · Appendices60Appendix F: What that error means18 min

Appendix F: What that error means#

Appendices · Chapter 60· 18 min read

The fastest way to lose confidence in a new platform is a stack trace that you cannot read. Each entry here gives the message as you will see it, what the message means in plain words, and the fix. Many entries also have a small example that triggers the error, folded under the entry. Paste an error into search (⌘K, or Ctrl+K), and search shows its entry here.

You need one distinction first. Java separates an Exception from an Error. Your code may reasonably catch an Exception. An Error means that the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) itself is in trouble. If the name of a class ends in Error, catching that class is almost always wrong.

Reading a Java stack trace#

Every entry below needs one skill, so start with that skill. Suppose that the shop's checkout fails because the payment provider never answers. OrderController calls OrderService. Then OrderService calls PaymentGatewayClient. The program prints this:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalStateException: payment provider did not answer
    at com.acme.payments.PaymentGatewayClient.charge(PaymentGatewayClient.java:20)
    at com.acme.orders.OrderService.place(OrderService.java:7)
    at com.acme.orders.OrderController.create(OrderController.java:6)
    at com.acme.orders.Main.main(Main.java:8)
Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out
    at java.base/sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl.timedRead(NioSocketImpl.java:276)
    at java.base/sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl.implRead(NioSocketImpl.java:302)
    at java.base/sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl.read(NioSocketImpl.java:360)
    at java.base/sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl$1.read(NioSocketImpl.java:802)
    at java.base/java.net.Socket$SocketInputStream.implRead(Socket.java:984)
    at java.base/java.net.Socket$SocketInputStream.read(Socket.java:974)
    at java.base/java.net.Socket$SocketInputStream.read(Socket.java:968)
    at com.acme.payments.PaymentGatewayClient.charge(PaymentGatewayClient.java:17)
    ... 3 more
Reading the code
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalStateException: payment provider did not answer

The first line names the exception, its message, and the thread where the exception happened.

at com.acme.payments.PaymentGatewayClient.charge(PaymentGatewayClient.java:20)

The top frame is the place where the exception was thrown. It gives the file and the line. Each line below the top frame is the method that called the method in the line above it. The list ends at main.

Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out

This is the exception that the first exception wrapped. The last Caused by: in a trace is usually the real problem. Here, the real problem is that the payment provider did not answer in time.

at java.base/sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl.timedRead(NioSocketImpl.java:276)

These frames are inside Java's own libraries. You can usually skip these frames and go to the first frame from your own code. Here that frame is PaymentGatewayClient.charge at line 17.

... 3 more

The last three frames are the same as the last three frames printed above, so Java does not print them again.

ConventionMeaning
Top framewhere the exception was thrown, not where it was caught
Caused bythe underlying exception, and the last Caused by in a trace is usually the real cause
... N moreframes shared with the enclosing trace, left out to save space
Suppressedan exception from close() that did not replace the primary one
java.base/the module the class came from, printed since Java 9
Note

Read a Java trace bottom up. In a wrapped exception, the deepest Caused by is the actual failure. Every part above it is a layer that threw the exception again. This is the reverse of the habit that most people bring from .NET. In .NET, the InnerException is nested, and it is not printed last.

The entries below are grouped by the place where you meet them. The groups are start-up, run time, the database, the web, the JVM itself and the compiler.

Spring Boot will not start#

Gotcha

Read the summary above the stack trace first. Spring Boot prints a short, readable explanation under a banner that reads APPLICATION FAILED TO START. This explanation is usually the whole answer. In the trace itself, the useful line is at the bottom, in the last Caused by:.

Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use.#
Means
Another program is already listening on the port that the embedded web server wants. Often the other program is an earlier run of the same application that is still running.
Fix
Stop the other program, or choose another port with server.port=8081.
What triggers it
java -jar target/app.jar &
java -jar target/app.jar     # The second copy finds port 8080 already taken.
NoSuchBeanDefinitionException: No qualifying bean of type 'com.acme.RatesClient' available#
Means
Something asked Spring for an object of this type. No bean provides one, so Spring never created the object.
Fix
Annotate the class with @Component or @Service. If the class is already annotated, move the class into the package of the application class, or into a package below that one. Then component scanning finds the class.
What triggers it
class RatesClient { }          // It has no annotation, so Spring never creates one.

@Service
class Pricing { Pricing(RatesClient rates) { } }
Parameter 0 of constructor in com.acme.Pricing required a bean of type 'com.acme.RatesClient' that could not be found. Action: Consider defining a bean of type 'com.acme.RatesClient' in your configuration.#
Means
This is the readable summary that Spring Boot prints for the problem in the entry before this one. No bean provides an object of the type that a constructor needs. The summary names the class, and the constructor parameter that needed the missing bean.
Fix
Annotate the class of the missing bean with @Component or @Service, or declare an @Bean method that returns an object of that type.
UnsatisfiedDependencyException: Error creating bean with name 'pricing'#
Means
Spring could not build a bean. The constructor of that bean needs other beans, and Spring could not build one of those beans. This exception only wraps the real cause.
Fix
Read the last Caused by: line. This line names the dependency that failed.
The dependencies of some of the beans in the application context form a cycle#
Means
Two beans each need the other bean in their constructor. So Spring cannot build either bean first. The underlying exception is BeanCurrentlyInCreationException.
Fix
Move the logic that the two beans share into a third bean. See Circular dependencies.
What triggers it
@Service class Orders  { Orders(Billing billing) { } }
@Service class Billing { Billing(Orders orders) { } }
Failed to configure a DataSource: 'url' attribute is not specified and no embedded datasource could be configured.#
Means
A Jakarta Persistence (JPA) or Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) starter is on the classpath, so Spring Boot expects a database. But no database is configured.
Fix
Set spring.datasource.url, or remove the starter until you need a database.
No qualifying bean of type 'com.acme.Pay' available: expected single matching bean but found 2: cardPayment,bankPayment#
Means
Two beans implement the type, and nothing tells Spring which bean to inject.
Fix
Mark one bean as @Primary, or name the bean that you want with @Qualifier("cardPayment") at the injection point.
What triggers it
@Service class CardPayment implements Pay { }
@Service class BankPayment implements Pay { }

@Service class Checkout { Checkout(Pay pay) { } }   // Which one? Spring cannot tell.

Common runtime exceptions#

java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.length()" because "c.name" is null#
Means
A null reference was used. Since Java 15 the message names the expression that was null. If the code was compiled without debugging information, a local variable appears as <local1> instead of its name.
Fix
Find the place where that value should have been set. To stop nulls from spreading, see the chapter Nullability.
What triggers it
var c = new Customer();     // Nothing sets c.name, so it is null.
c.name.length();
java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.String cannot be cast to class java.lang.Integer#
Means
A cast named the wrong type at run time. With generics, type erasure can move the failure far from the line that caused it.
Fix
Test the real type with instanceof before you cast. Also search earlier in the code for a raw type or an unchecked warning.
What triggers it
Object o = "x";
Integer i = (Integer) o;
java.util.ConcurrentModificationException#
Means
A collection was changed while a loop was iterating over it. By chance, removing the second-to-last element does not throw, so a test with two items can miss the bug.
Fix
Use removeIf, or use an explicit Iterator and call its remove() method. See Modifying while iterating.
What triggers it
var names = new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b", "c"));
for (var n : names) names.remove(n);     // This throws on the second time round.
java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException#
Means
Code tried to add an element to a collection, or to remove an element from it, and the collection does not allow that. An example is a collection made by List.of or Arrays.asList.
Fix
Copy the collection into a mutable collection first, with new ArrayList<>(List.of(...)).
What triggers it
List.of(1).add(2);
java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: "12a"#
Means
Text could not be parsed as a number. Java has no TryParse, so the parse throws.
Fix
Catch NumberFormatException where the input comes from a user, or validate the input first.
What triggers it
Integer.parseInt("12a");
java.lang.ArrayStoreException: java.lang.Integer#
Means
An array that is declared as Object[] really holds a narrower type. A value of the wrong type was stored in the array.
Fix
Use a List<T>. Generics are checked at compile time, but arrays are checked only at run time.
What triggers it
Object[] items = new String[1];
items[0] = 1;
java.lang.IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed#
Means
A stream was used twice. A stream can be consumed only once. In C#, you can enumerate an IEnumerable again.
Fix
Create a new stream for each pass, or collect the stream to a List once and reuse that list.
What triggers it
var s = List.of(1, 2).stream();
s.toList();
s.toList();     // The second call throws.
java.lang.IllegalStateException: block()/blockFirst()/blockLast() are blocking, which is not supported in thread parallel-2#
Means
Code on one of Reactor's own non-blocking threads called block(). The name of the thread is at the end of the message, and it varies.
Fix
Return the Mono, or chain the next step with map or flatMap. See the full entry.
java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero#
Means
The code divided an integer by zero. Division on double gives Infinity and does not throw.
Fix
Check the divisor first, or divide as double if Infinity is acceptable.
java.time.format.DateTimeParseException: Text '11/09/2026' could not be parsed at index 0#
Means
The text does not match the pattern. LocalDate.parse expects ISO format, such as 2026-09-11.
Fix
Pass a DateTimeFormatter with the right pattern. The pattern letters in Java differ from the pattern letters in .NET, so check them.
What triggers it
LocalDate.parse("11/09/2026");
LocalDate.parse("11/09/2026", DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("dd/MM/yyyy"));   // This works.
java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: src/main/resources/rates.json#
Means
The code read a resource as a file on disk. That path exists in the project folder, but it does not exist beside a packaged Java archive (JAR).
Fix
Read the resource through the classpath. See the full entry.
Cannot invoke "java.io.InputStream.readAllBytes()" because "in" is null#
Means
getResourceAsStream found nothing under that name. It returned null and did not throw.
Fix
Check the name and its leading slash. See the full entry.

Persistence#

org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: failed to lazily initialize a collection of role: com.acme.Order.items: could not initialize proxy - no Session#
Means
Hibernate loads some related data lazily, which means only when the data is first read. Here the data was first read after its transaction had closed, usually in a controller. The message above is the wording of Hibernate 6.6, which Spring Boot 3.4 uses. For the wording of Hibernate 7, see the next entry. For a single entity, both versions print Could not initialize proxy [com.acme.Customer#7] - no session.
Fix
Fetch what you need inside the transaction, with JOIN FETCH or @EntityGraph. Or map the data to a data transfer object (DTO) inside the transaction. See Lazy loading.
What triggers it
Order order = orderService.find(7);   // The transaction ends when find returns.
order.getItems().size();              // Too late: the session is already closed.
org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: Cannot lazily initialize collection of role 'com.acme.Order.items' with key '7' (no session)#
Means
This is the same late read of a lazy collection as in the entry before this one. A lazy collection was first read after its transaction had closed. The message is in the wording of Hibernate 7, which Spring Boot 4 uses. The key in the message is the id of the order that owns the collection.
Fix
Fetch what you need inside the transaction, or map the data to a DTO inside the transaction. See Lazy loading.
jakarta.persistence.TransactionRequiredException: No EntityManager with actual transaction available for current thread - cannot reliably process 'persist' call#
Means
A write used the shared EntityManager while no transaction was running.
Fix
Put @Transactional on the service method that makes the change.
org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException: could not execute statement#
Means
The database rejected a write because of a constraint. The constraint is a unique key, a foreign key, or a NOT NULL column.
Fix
Read the Caused by: line for the name of the constraint. Then fix the data or the mapping.
ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException: Row was updated or deleted by another transaction (or unsaved-value mapping was incorrect)#
Means
The @Version check failed. This means that someone else changed the row after you read it. The message above is the wording of Hibernate 6.6, which Spring Boot 3.4 uses. On Spring Boot 4, Hibernate 7 prints Row was already updated or deleted by another transaction, followed by the entity.
Fix
Reload and retry, or tell the user their copy is out of date.
ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException: Row was already updated or deleted by another transaction for entity [com.acme.Order with id '1']#
Means
This is the same failed @Version check as in the entry before this one. Someone else changed the row after you read it. The message is in the wording of Hibernate 7, which Spring Boot 4 uses.
Fix
Reload and retry, or tell the user their copy is out of date.
detached entity passed to persist: com.acme.Order#
Means
persist was called on an object that already has an id, so Hibernate treats the object as a row that already exists. On Spring Boot 4, Hibernate 7 writes the same message with a capital D.
Fix
Use merge. Or use save on a Spring Data repository, which chooses between persist and merge. Do not set a generated id yourself.
No identifier specified for entity: com.acme.Order#
Means
A class marked @Entity has no field marked @Id. The message above is the wording of Hibernate 5 and 6.0. Hibernate 6.1 and later print the message in the next entry. So the Hibernate of Spring Boot 3.4 and the Hibernate of Spring Boot 4 both print that message.
Fix
Add an @Id field, usually with @GeneratedValue.
Entity 'com.acme.Order' has no identifier (every '@Entity' class must declare or inherit at least one '@Id' or '@EmbeddedId' property)#
Means
A class marked @Entity has no field marked @Id. This is the wording since Hibernate 6.1. On Spring Boot 4, Hibernate 7 printed this message in a run.
Fix
Add an @Id field, usually with @GeneratedValue.

The next entries belong to document data. The first entry and the last two entries are quoted from the AWS developer guide, as of October 2026. The other entries were produced on 3 October 2026 against a MongoDB container, not against Amazon DocumentDB.

{"ok":0,"errmsg":"Retryable writes are not supported","code":301,"name":"MongoError"}#
Means
Amazon DocumentDB rejected a write that the driver marked as retryable. Drivers mark writes as retryable by default. Engine versions before 8.0.2 and elastic clusters do not support retryable writes. The message is the server's reply as AWS prints it. The Java exception around the reply was not run.
Fix
Add retryWrites=false to the connection string, or move an instance-based cluster to engine version 8.0.2. See Connecting to Amazon DocumentDB.
What triggers it
spring:
  mongodb:
    uri: mongodb://sample-user:password@sample-cluster.node.us-east-1.docdb.amazonaws.com:27017/shop?replicaSet=rs0
com.mongodb.MongoTimeoutException: Timed out while waiting for a server that matches ReadPreferenceServerSelector{readPreference=primary}. Client view of cluster state is {type=UNKNOWN, servers=[{address=localhost:27019, type=UNKNOWN, state=CONNECTING, exception={com.mongodb.MongoSocketWriteException: Exception sending message}, caused by {javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: (certificate_unknown) PKIX path building failed: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException: unable to find valid certification path to requested target}#
Means
The server's certificate was signed by a certificate authority that this Java program does not trust. The driver reports every failed connection as a MongoTimeoutException, so read the message as far as the innermost caused by.
Fix
Give the program the certificates of the authority, through an SSL bundle or a trust store. For Amazon DocumentDB, the certificates are in the file global-bundle.pem. A tlsCAFile parameter in the connection string changed nothing in the run. See Connecting to Amazon DocumentDB.
What triggers it
spring:
  mongodb:
    uri: mongodb://localhost:27019/shop?tls=true     # no spring.mongodb.ssl.bundle
com.mongodb.MongoSocketReadException: Prematurely reached end of stream#
Means
The program connected without Transport Layer Security (TLS) to a server that accepts only TLS, and the server closed the connection. The message is inside a MongoTimeoutException, as in the entry before this one.
Fix
Enable TLS. To do this, name an SSL bundle in spring.mongodb.ssl.bundle, or add tls=true to the connection string.
org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException: Write operation error on MongoDB server localhost:27018. Write error: WriteError{code=11000, message='E11000 duplicate key error collection: shop.invoices index: orderId dup key: { orderId: "o-1" }', details={}}.#
Means
A unique index rejected a second document with the same value. The same exception can appear at startup, with the words Index build failed. Then it means that auto index creation tried to build a unique index over documents that already hold duplicates.
Fix
Handle the exception where a duplicate is possible. For the startup failure, remove the duplicates before you enable index creation. See Indexes.
What triggers it
// spring.data.mongodb.auto-index-creation is true, and orderId is @Indexed(unique = true)
invoices.save(new Invoice(null, "o-1", total, today));
invoices.save(new Invoice(null, "o-1", total, today));
org.springframework.data.mongodb.UncategorizedMongoDbException: This MongoDB deployment does not support retryable writes. Please add retryWrites=false to your connection string.#
Means
A transaction started on a MongoDB server that is not a replica set. In the run, that server was the container that a plain new MongoDBContainer("mongo:8.0") starts in a test.
Fix
Start the test's container with .withReplicaSet(). See Developing and testing without a cluster.
Given transaction number 0 does not match any in-progress transactions.#
Means
This is error 251 from Amazon DocumentDB. AWS states that this error follows one of two events. The first event is a transaction that ran longer than the one-minute limit and was aborted. The second event is a restart of the instance.
Fix
Keep the transaction short, and make its writes safe to repeat. See the documented limits.
Feature not supported: 'causal consistency'#
Means
This is error 303 from Amazon DocumentDB, which does not support causal consistency. AWS shows a read that fails with this error in a session started with the default options (as of October 2026). The message is quoted from AWS, and it was not run.
Fix
AWS's own examples turn causal consistency off when they start the session. They use ClientSessionOptions.builder().causallyConsistent(false).build(). Spring's MongoTransactionManager opens a causally consistent session. No test checked whether Amazon DocumentDB rejects that session, so test a @Transactional method on your cluster. See Transactions.

Web and JSON#

HttpMessageNotReadableException: JSON parse error: Cannot deserialize value of type `int` from String "abc"#
Means
The request body could not be converted to the parameter's type. The cause is malformed JSON, or a value of the wrong type.
Fix
Compare the JSON with the components of the record. The message names the value and the type.
MethodArgumentNotValidException: Validation failed for argument [0]#
Means
Bean Validation rejected a @Valid request body, and Spring answers with a 400.
Fix
This is usually the 400 that you want. Shape the body of the response in a @RestControllerAdvice. See field-level errors.
InvalidDefinitionException: No serializer found for class com.acme.Empty and no properties discovered to create BeanSerializer#
Means
Jackson found nothing that it could write for a type. The type has no getters and no public fields, or the object is a lazy Hibernate proxy. For a class with nothing to write, only Jackson 2 on Spring Boot 3 throws this exception. On Spring Boot 4, Jackson 3 writes {} instead.
Fix
Return a record or a DTO in place of the entity, or give the class getters.
UnrecognizedPropertyException: Unrecognized field "extra" (class com.acme.Order), not marked as ignorable#
Means
The JSON has a property that the target type does not have, and the mapper is set to fail on an unknown property. Jackson 2 fails on an unknown property by default. Jackson 3 and the mapper that Spring Boot builds do not fail on one by default.
Fix
Add the field, or annotate the type with @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true). On a mapper that you build yourself, you can also disable FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES.
HttpMediaTypeNotSupportedException: Content-Type 'text/plain;charset=UTF-8' is not supported#
Means
The request's Content-Type does not match what the endpoint consumes.
Fix
Send Content-Type: application/json, or widen the mapping's consumes.
MissingServletRequestParameterException: Required request parameter 'q' for method parameter type String is not present#
Means
A @RequestParam was missing from the request, and request parameters are required by default.
Fix
Send the parameter, or declare it with required = false or a defaultValue. See Model binding.
403 Forbidden on a POST, with an empty response body#
Means
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection rejected a request that changes state, because the request carried no CSRF token.
Fix
For a stateless API that authenticates with a token, disable CSRF in the security chain. Otherwise, send the CSRF token. See Two chain traps: rule order and CSRF.

Errors, not exceptions#

For a worked example of each of the first five entries, see the chapter How Java runs your code.

java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: com/acme/App has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 69.0)#
Means
The code was built for a newer Java than the Java that runs it. Subtract 44 from the class file version to get the release. So version 69 is Java 25.
Fix
Make the build's target match the runtime image. See the full entry.
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: com/acme/Greeter#
Means
A class that was present at compile time is missing at run time. The cause is a packaging problem, or a dependency scope that excludes the class.
Fix
Put the class, or its Java archive (JAR), back on the classpath. See the full entry.
java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.postgresql.Driver#
Means
A lookup by name found nothing. The lookup is usually Class.forName, or a class named in configuration. This exception is a checked exception, unlike NoClassDefFoundError, which is an error.
Fix
Add the dependency with a run-time scope. See the full entry.
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.String com.acme.Greeter.greet(java.lang.String)'#
Means
The class was found, but it is a different version from the version that your code was compiled against.
Fix
Run mvn dependency:tree to find the two versions, and pin one version. See the full entry.
java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError#
Means
A static initialiser threw an exception. Every later use of the class fails with NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class.
Fix
Read the Caused by: line for the real exception. See the full entry.
java.lang.IncompatibleClassChangeError: Expected static method 'void Util.go()'#
Means
A class changed shape after its callers were compiled. A static method became an instance method, or a class became an interface.
Fix
The cause is the same as the cause of NoSuchMethodError. Build against one version, and ship that same version.
What triggers it
# App calls the static Util.go(). Then Util is changed and recompiled on its own.
javac Util.java App.java
sed -i '' 's/static //' Util.java && javac Util.java
java App
java.lang.StackOverflowError#
Means
Recursion went too deep. Often the cause is two entities that call each other's toString, equals or hashCode.
Fix
Find the frames that repeat at the top of the trace, and break the cycle.
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space#
Means
The heap is full, and the garbage collector could not free enough to continue.
Fix
Capture a heap dump with -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError, and find the leak before you raise -Xmx.
What triggers it
var keep = new ArrayList<long[]>();
while (true) keep.add(new long[1_000_000]);    // Run with -Xmx16m to see it quickly.
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace#
Means
Class metadata filled its space. The usual cause is a class loader leak from repeated redeploys or from generated classes.
Fix
Set -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize so that the program fails early. Then find what keeps loading classes.
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread: possibly out of memory or process/resource limits reached#
Means
The operating system refused to create another platform thread. The cause is too many threads, or a process limit.
Fix
Run work that waits on input and output on virtual threads, or put a limit on the pool.

Compiler messages#

error: cannot find symbol#
Means
The compiler does not know a name. The cause is a missing import, a typo, or a class that is not on the classpath.
Fix
Read the symbol: and location: lines under the message. In IntelliJ, Alt+Enter usually adds the missing import. On a Mac, the keys are ⌥↩.
What triggers it
Lst<String> names;        // The compiler reports "symbol: class Lst".
error: unreported exception IOException; must be caught or declared to be thrown#
Means
A checked exception is not caught and is not declared.
Fix
Catch the exception, add throws to the method, or wrap the exception. See Checked exceptions.
What triggers it
void load() { Files.readString(Path.of("rates.json")); }
error: incompatible types: possible lossy conversion from long to int#
Means
Java will not narrow a number silently.
Fix
Cast explicitly after you check that the value fits. Or use Math.toIntExact, which throws if the value does not fit.
What triggers it
long total = 1;
int count = total;
error: variable x might not have been initialized#
Means
A local variable could be read on some path before any value was assigned.
Fix
Assign the variable on every path, or give it an initial value.
What triggers it
int x;
if (ready) x = 1;
System.out.println(x);
error: local variables referenced from a lambda expression must be final or effectively final#
Means
A lambda captures a local variable that is reassigned somewhere.
Fix
Use an AtomicInteger or AtomicReference, or change the code so that the variable is assigned only once.
What triggers it
int n = 0;
Runnable r = () -> n++;
error: non-static variable x cannot be referenced from a static context#
Means
Instance state was used from a static method, most often main.
Fix
Create an instance and use it, or make the member static if it truly belongs to the class.
What triggers it
class App {
    int x;
    public static void main(String[] args) { x = 1; }
}
error: class A is public, should be declared in a file named A.java#
Means
A public class must be in a file that has exactly the name of the class.
Fix
Rename the file or the class so that the file name and the class name match.
error: bad operand types for binary operator '>'#
Means
An operator was used on types that do not support it, usually > or < on strings or other objects.
Fix
Use compareTo to order objects, and use equals to compare them. See the chapter Equality and hashing.
What triggers it
boolean later = name > "m";
error: reached end of file while parsing#
Means
A brace or parenthesis was opened and never closed.
Fix
Let the IDE highlight the unmatched brace. The IDE finds the brace faster than javac does.
error: find(String) in EmptyLookup cannot implement find(String) in PriceLookup attempting to assign weaker access privileges; was public#
Means
A method that implements an interface method has no public keyword. In a class, a method with no access keyword is package-private. Package-private is less visible than the interface's method.
Fix
Write public on the implementing method. See the full entry.

When something breaks
SymptomLook at
Could not find or load main classclasspath, or package and folder mismatch
Annotation does nothingself-invocation, private, or final method

Note

One simple rule explains most of the traps column. Java makes the safe thing explicit and the unsafe thing the default more often than C# does. Reference equality, package-private access, virtual methods and ORDINAL enum mapping are all defaults. To get the safe behaviour, you must write it explicitly.

Most traps on the card are predictions. Each prediction is in the chapter The week-one gotchas or in the chapter for its own subject. So each prediction is also a card in Review. Press r to be asked the question instead of being told the answer.

If a term on the card is unfamiliar, especially the classpath, start with the chapter How Java runs your code.
