Appendix H: Java words in plain English#

Appendices · Chapter 62· 25 min read

This appendix explains each Java word the book uses, in plain words, and links to the section that teaches it. You do not need to read it in order. Search for a word, or come here when a word in a chapter is new to you.

Every entry gives the word, what it means in a few short sentences, and where the book explains it in full. If Java uses a word differently from .NET, the meaning says so. Abbreviations are listed under their short form, such as JVM (Java Virtual Machine), with the full name first in the meaning.

TermWhat it meansWhere it is explained
ActuatorThe Spring Boot module that adds health, metrics and information endpoints to a service, such as /actuator/health.Actuator endpoints
AMQPShort for Advanced Message Queuing Protocol. It is the wire protocol that RabbitMQ uses.RabbitMQ
annotationA marker written with @ before a class, method, field or parameter, such as @Override. It does the same as an attribute in C#.Syntax
annotation processorA plug-in that the Java compiler runs during a build. It reads annotations and generates extra source files. It does the same as a source generator in C#.Annotation processing vs source generators
annotation retentionHow long an annotation is kept. An annotation is kept only in the source, or in the class file, or at runtime. Reflection can read an annotation that is kept at runtime. C# attributes are always there at runtime.Retention: the concept C# lacks
AOPShort for aspect-oriented programming. It is a way of adding behaviour, such as logging or transactions, around many methods without editing each one. Spring does it with proxies.AOP: writing your own cross-cutting behaviour
AOTShort for ahead-of-time. It is work that is done when the application is built, not when the application runs. Two examples are compiling to native code and preparing a startup cache.GraalVM native-image
AOT cacheA file that the JVM writes during a training run and reads on later starts, so classes load and link faster. It shortens startup without a native image.Startup without going native
application contextThe Spring container. It is the object that creates your beans, connects them to each other and gives them to the code that asks for them. It does the same as IServiceProvider in .NET.The bean lifecycle
application eventA message that one part of a Spring application publishes and other parts receive, in the same process. It is like a MediatR notification in .NET.Application events
application serverA large server, such as WildFly or WebSphere, that runs many deployed applications. The applications are deployed as web application archive (WAR) or enterprise archive (EAR) files. Spring Boot services usually embed their own server instead.EJB and the application server
aspectA class marked @Aspect. It holds behaviour that Spring applies around many methods, such as timing every service call.AOP: writing your own cross-cutting behaviour
AssertJThe assertion library that most Java tests use. An assertion is written assertThat(actual).isEqualTo(expected). AssertJ is like FluentAssertions in .NET.A test
@AsyncA Spring annotation that runs a method on another thread, so the caller does not wait for the method. It works only when the call goes through a Spring proxy.@Async
atomic variableA class such as AtomicInteger. Its operations, such as incrementAndGet, are safe to call from many threads at once without a lock. An atomic variable is like Interlocked in .NET.Atomics
auto-configurationSpring Boot creating suitable beans for you, such as a database connection pool. Spring Boot creates a bean because a library is on the classpath and you have not defined that bean yourself.Auto-configuration
autoboxingJava automatically converting between a primitive, such as int, and its wrapper object, such as Integer. Unboxing a null wrapper throws a NullPointerException.Wrapper types
@BeanAn annotation that marks a method in a configuration class. Spring manages the return value of the method as a bean. Use @Bean for types that you cannot annotate yourself, such as a client class from a library.Beans for types you do not own
beanAn object that Spring creates and manages, and can inject into other objects. It is what you would register in a .NET service collection.Beans and component scanning
bean scopeHow many instances of a bean Spring makes. The default scope is called singleton, and it means one instance for the whole application. The scope called prototype means a new instance each time the bean is asked for.Lifetimes
Bean ValidationThe Java standard for validation annotations such as @NotBlank and @Size. It has the same purpose as DataAnnotations in .NET.Validation and error responses
BeanPostProcessorAn object that Spring passes every bean to while the bean is created. This object can change, wrap or replace the bean. Spring uses one such object to put proxies around beans with annotations such as @Transactional.The bean lifecycle
BigDecimalThe Java class for exact decimal numbers, used for money. It is a class, so you add with add() and not with +. You compare with compareTo() and not with >.Money is BigDecimal
BOMShort for bill of materials. It is a Maven file that sets the versions of many related libraries at once, so the libraries stay compatible. In a text file, BOM can also mean byte order mark.Profiles and BOMs
BSONThe format in which MongoDB and Amazon DocumentDB store a document. It has types that JSON does not have, such as ObjectId, Date and Decimal128. The .NET attributes such as [BsonId] are named after it.What the stored document holds: types, names and _class
BuildpacksA tool that turns an application into a container image without a Dockerfile. The build-image task of Spring Boot uses it.Containers
bytecodeThe instructions that the Java compiler javac produces from your source code. The JVM runs bytecode in the same way that the .NET runtime runs IL.From source to a running program
@CacheableA Spring annotation that stores the result of a method. A second call with the same arguments returns the stored value without running the method.Caching
CASShort for compare-and-set. It is an operation that changes a value only if the value is still what you expected. The check and the change happen as one step that cannot be divided. Atomic classes use compare-and-set instead of a lock.Atomics
CDSShort for class data sharing. It is a feature of the JVM. The JVM stores already-parsed classes in a file and maps the file into memory at startup, so the program starts faster.Startup without going native
CGLIBShort for Code Generation Library. It is the library that Spring uses to create a proxy as a subclass of your class at runtime. Spring Boot uses it by default, even for a bean that implements an interface.Two kinds of proxy
charsetThe encoding that turns text into bytes and back, such as UTF-8. Java 18 and later use UTF-8 by default. Passing a charset explicitly keeps older code correct too.Charsets, and why to always pass one
checked exceptionAn exception that the compiler makes you handle. You must catch it, or declare it with throws. C# has no checked exceptions.Checked exceptions
class fileA file ending in .class that holds the bytecode of one class. The compiler writes one class file for each class.From source to a running program
class loaderThe part of the JVM that finds a class the first time your code uses the class, and reads the bytecode of the class.Class loading, at the level you need
classpathThe ordered list of folders and Java archive (JAR) files that the JVM searches when it needs a class. The JVM uses the first match.The classpath is a search list
classpath resourceA file that is packaged with your classes, such as a configuration file or a template. Code reads it through the classpath, not from a path on disk.Resources live on the classpath too
CMEShort for ConcurrentModificationException. It is thrown when a collection is changed while a loop over that collection is still running, even on a single thread.Modifying while iterating
compact constructorA record constructor that is written without a parameter list. It is used to check or adjust the values before they are stored.Checking values: the compact constructor
ComparatorAn object that decides the order of two values, like IComparer<T> in C#. The natural order of a class itself comes from Comparable, which is like IComparable<T> in C#.Ordering
CompletableFutureThe Java class that is closest to Task<T> in C#. It holds a result that arrives later. It has methods such as thenApply that chain more work onto the result.Translation
component scanningSpring searching your packages at startup for classes marked @Component, @Service and similar annotations. Spring registers each class that it finds as a bean.Beans and component scanning
@ConfigurationPropertiesAn annotation that binds a group of settings from application.yml to the fields of a class or record. In ASP.NET Core, IOptions<T> binds a section in the same way.IOptions becomes @ConfigurationProperties
constructor injectionGiving a class what it needs through its constructor parameters. Spring provides the values when it creates an object of the class. Constructor injection is the recommended style, and ASP.NET Core uses the same style.Beans and component scanning
controller adviceA class of exception handlers that apply to every controller. It is used to turn exceptions into error responses in one place.Global exception handling
coroutineThe lightweight form of concurrency in Kotlin. A coroutine is a function marked suspend that can pause without blocking a thread. It is close to async and await in C#.Coroutines against virtual threads
CORSShort for cross-origin resource sharing. It is the browser rule that decides whether a web page may call an API on another domain. The server allows the call with response headers.Middleware
CSRFShort for cross-site request forgery. It is another site making a user's browser send a request with that user's cookies. Spring Security blocks it by default for requests that change data.Two chain traps: rule order and CSRF
dependency scopeA setting on a Maven dependency that says when the dependency is available. compile means everywhere, and test means tests only. runtime and provided are for the cases in between.Coordinates
detached entityAn entity that was loaded by a persistence context that is now closed. Changes to the entity are no longer tracked, and its lazy fields can no longer load.Lazy loading and detached entities
DIShort for dependency injection. It means that a class receives the objects it needs, usually through its constructor, and does not create them itself. Spring and ASP.NET Core both do dependency injection.Dependency injection and configuration
DSLShort for domain-specific language. It is a small, focused way of writing one kind of thing, often as a chain of method calls. One example is the configuration of Spring Security.The filter chain
DTOShort for data transfer object. It is a simple class, often a record, that carries data in or out of an API without exposing your entities.Records as DTOs
EARShort for enterprise archive. It is a file that packages several WAR and JAR files for an application server. You will only see it in older systems.EJB and the application server
EJBShort for Enterprise JavaBeans. It is the component model of the old Java EE application servers. Spring replaced it in most new code.EJB and the application server
entityA class marked @Entity that Jakarta Persistence maps to a database table. It is like an entity in Entity Framework.An entity
enumA type with a fixed set of named values. In Java each value is a full object, so an enum can have fields, constructors and methods.The shape of the difference
ExecutorServiceAn object that runs tasks on threads that it manages. For example, it can use a fixed pool of threads, or one virtual thread for each task. You submit work and receive a Future.Fixed thread pools
fat JAROne JAR file that holds your application and every library that the application needs, so java -jar app.jar runs it. Spring Boot builds a fat JAR by default.The fat JAR
final fieldThe keyword final means that a thing cannot change after it is set. A final field or variable is assigned once. A final class cannot be extended, and a final method cannot be overridden.final is not readonly, quite
FlywayA tool that runs numbered SQL migration scripts against the database at startup. It has the same purpose as EF Core migrations in .NET. Liquibase is the main alternative.Migrations
fully qualified nameA class name with its package in front, such as com.acme.billing.Invoice. The JVM uses this name to find the class file.One program, start to finish
functional interfaceAn interface with exactly one method to implement, such as Runnable or Function<T, R>. You can write a lambda in its place, as you write a lambda for a delegate in C#.Lambdas and method references
G1The default garbage collector of the JVM on most machines. It balances short pauses against throughput.Choosing a collector
gathererA custom step that is added to a stream with gather(). It is for operations that are not built in, such as sliding windows. It is final since Java 24.Gatherers
GCShort for garbage collector. It is the part of the JVM that frees memory that no object uses any more. The JVM offers several garbage collectors, such as G1 and ZGC.Choosing a collector
GraalVMA Java Development Kit (JDK) that can compile a Java application ahead of time into a native executable. The native executable starts in milliseconds, but it limits reflection.GraalVM native-image
GradleA Java build tool, and the main alternative to Maven. Its build files are written in a small Groovy or Kotlin language, not in XML.Gradle against Maven
happens-beforeThe rule in the Java memory model for when one thread is guaranteed to see the writes of another thread. For example, the guarantee holds after a lock is released or after a volatile field is written.volatile means more in Java
health indicatorA small class that reports whether one dependency, such as the database, is up. Actuator combines all health indicators into /actuator/health. This is like health checks in ASP.NET Core.Custom health checks
heapThe memory where the JVM keeps objects. Its maximum size is set with -Xmx, or as a share of a container's memory.The memory model
HibernateThe most widely used implementation of Jakarta Persistence, and the implementation that Spring Boot uses by default.The landscape
HQLShort for Hibernate Query Language. It is the query language of Hibernate, and a superset of the Jakarta Persistence Query Language (JPQL). Queries are written against entities, not against tables.Repositories
initialiser blockA block of code in a class body. A static initialiser block runs when the class is loaded. An instance initialiser block runs when an object is created. C# has static constructors instead.Initialiser blocks
inner classA class declared inside another class without static. Each instance holds a hidden reference to the outer object. A nested class in C# holds no such reference.Inner classes capture the outer instance
Integer cacheJava keeps ready-made Integer objects for the values -128 to 127. So == on two small Integers can be true, while the same code on larger numbers is false.The Integer cache
IoCShort for inversion of control. It means that the framework, not your code, creates objects and calls their methods. Dependency injection is the most common form.Beans and component scanning
isolation levelHow much one transaction may see of the unfinished changes of another transaction. One level is READ_COMMITTED. Isolation levels are the same database idea as in .NET.Isolation
J2EEShort for Java 2 Platform, Enterprise Edition. It is the old name for enterprise Java. The name later became Java EE, and it is now Jakarta EE.Four eras
JacksonThe JSON library that Spring Boot uses by default. It does the same as System.Text.Json in .NET.Jackson against System.Text.Json
Jakarta EEThe set of enterprise Java standards, such as Persistence, Validation and Servlet. Its old name is Java EE. Its packages moved from javax to jakarta.The javax to jakarta rename
JARShort for Java archive. It is a zip file of class files and resources, usually with a manifest. It does the same as a .dll assembly in .NET.Running with -cp or -jar
Java moduleA named group of packages, described in a module-info.java file. The file states what the module exports and what the module needs. Most applications never write a module.The problem it solves
java.timeThe package of date and time types added in Java 8, such as LocalDate and Instant. Use it for all new code instead of Date and Calendar.java.time
JAXBShort for Jakarta XML Binding. It is the standard for turning XML into Java objects and back. It was removed from the JDK in Java 11 and is now a separate library.What Java removed
JDBCShort for Java Database Connectivity. It is the low-level standard for talking to a database, like ADO.NET. Jakarta Persistence and the JdbcClient of Spring are built on it.The landscape
JDKShort for Java Development Kit. It is the compiler, the JVM and the tools that you need to build and run Java. It is like the .NET SDK.JDK or JRE: which to install
JEPShort for JDK Enhancement Proposal. It is the numbered document that describes one change to Java, such as JEP 444 for virtual threads.The release train
JFRShort for JDK Flight Recorder. It is a low-overhead recorder built into the JVM. It captures what a running program is doing, for later analysis.JFR: the recorder built into the JDK
JITShort for just-in-time compiler. It is the part of the JVM that compiles frequently run bytecode to machine code while the program runs. RyuJIT does the same in .NET.The JIT and warmup
jlinkA JDK tool that builds a trimmed Java runtime, which contains only the modules that your application needs.jlink and jpackage
JMHShort for Java Microbenchmark Harness. It is the standard tool for measuring small pieces of Java code. It does the same as BenchmarkDotNet in .NET.JMH against BenchmarkDotNet
JMSShort for Jakarta Messaging. It is a standard Java API for sending and receiving messages through a broker such as ActiveMQ. Kafka and RabbitMQ are usually used through their own Spring clients.JMS and JmsClient
JMXShort for Java Management Extensions. It is built into the JVM, and it exposes the metrics and operations of a running program to monitoring tools.Actuator endpoints
JNDIShort for Java Naming and Directory Interface. It is a lookup service that old application servers used to provide resources such as database connections.Single values and precedence
JNIShort for Java Native Interface. It is the way that Java code calls native C or C++ code, like P/Invoke in .NET.When virtual threads are the wrong tool
JPAShort for Jakarta Persistence. It is the Java standard for mapping objects to database tables. It has the same purpose as Entity Framework in .NET. Hibernate implements Jakarta Persistence.Data access, JPA and migrations
jpackageA JDK tool that wraps an application and a Java runtime into a native installer, such as an .msi or a .dmg.jlink and jpackage
JPMSShort for Java Platform Module System. It is the module system that was added in Java 9. It lets a library hide its internal packages.Modules, JPMS and the missing internal
JPQLShort for Jakarta Persistence Query Language. It is a language for SQL-like queries that are written against entities and their fields, not against tables and columns.Repositories
JREShort for Java Runtime Environment. It is a JVM and its libraries without the compiler. Oracle stopped shipping a separate JRE in Java 11, but some vendors, such as Temurin, still offer one.JDK or JRE: which to install
JShellThe Java read-eval-print loop (REPL). You type a line of Java and see the result immediately, without a class or a main method.jshell: run one line of Java
JSPShort for JavaServer Pages. It is an old way of writing HTML pages with Java code inside them, like classic ASP. Modern Spring uses templates or a separate front end.Web frameworks, in order of extinction
JSpecifyA standard set of annotations, such as @Nullable, that mark which values may be null. With them, tools can warn in the same way as nullable reference types in C#.JSpecify: the annotation standard
JSRShort for Java Specification Request. It is a numbered proposal for a Java standard. One example is JSR 305, an older attempt at null annotations.Null-safety in the Spring API
JUnitThe standard Java testing framework. It does the same as xUnit in .NET. A test is a method marked @Test.A test
JVMShort for Java Virtual Machine. It is the program that loads bytecode and runs it, in the same way that the CLR runs IL in .NET.From source to a running program
JWTShort for JSON Web Token. It is a signed token that carries the identity and claims of a user. It is sent in the Authorization header. It works the same way as in ASP.NET Core.Concept mapping
KotlinA language from JetBrains that runs on the JVM and uses Java libraries directly. Many C# developers find the syntax of Kotlin closer to C# than the syntax of Java.What Kotlin gives back that Java took away
lambdaA short unnamed function written with an arrow, such as x -> x * 2. C# writes =>. Java writes ->.Lambdas and method references
lazy loadingLoading the related data of an entity only when you first use that data. If the persistence context has closed by then, Hibernate throws LazyInitializationException.Lazy loading and detached entities
lifecycle phaseOne step of a Maven build, such as compile, test or package. When you run a phase, Maven first runs every phase before it.The lifecycle
local repositoryThe folder ~/.m2/repository, where Maven keeps every library that it downloads. It is like the NuGet global packages folder.Where your dependencies actually live
LogbackThe logging library that Spring Boot uses by default. Your code logs through the Simple Logging Facade for Java (SLF4J), and Logback writes the output.logback-spring.xml and JSON logging
LombokA library that generates getters, setters, constructors and similar code from annotations when you compile. Records remove much of the need for Lombok.A word on Lombok
LTSShort for long-term support. An LTS release is a Java release that vendors keep patching for years. Java 21 and Java 25 are LTS releases.The release train
manifestA small text file inside a JAR, at META-INF/MANIFEST.MF. It can name the class that holds main, and it can list other JARs to load.Inside a JAR: the manifest
MapStructA library that generates object-to-object mapping code when you compile. It has the same purpose as AutoMapper in .NET.MapStruct against AutoMapper
MavenThe most common Java build tool. It reads a pom.xml file and downloads the libraries listed there. Then it compiles, tests and packages the project. It is like MSBuild with NuGet in .NET.pom.xml against csproj
Maven coordinatesThe three values that identify a library in Maven. They are groupId for the organisation, artifactId for the library, and version. They are like the package id and version of a NuGet package.Coordinates
Maven profileA named set of settings in pom.xml that you switch on for some builds only, with mvn -P name.Profiles and BOMs
Maven wrapperThe mvnw script in a project. It downloads and runs the right Maven version, so everyone builds with the same version.The wrapper
MDCShort for mapped diagnostic context. It is a set of key and value pairs, such as a request id, that are attached to the current thread. Every log line then includes them. A mapped diagnostic context is like ILogger scopes in .NET.Logging
metaspaceThe memory outside the heap where the JVM keeps class definitions. Loading very many classes can use all of it.The memory model
method referenceA short way to pass an existing method where a lambda is expected. It is written Type::method, such as String::length.Lambdas and method references
MicrometerThe metrics library that Spring Boot uses. It does the same as System.Diagnostics.Metrics in .NET. It sends counters and timers to Prometheus and other systems.Metrics
MockitoThe standard Java library for mock objects. It does the same as Moq in .NET.Mocking
MockMvcA Spring test helper that sends fake HTTP requests to your controllers without starting a server.Testing a controller
module pathThe list of modules that the JVM loads when the module system is switched on. It is like the classpath, but for modules.Classpath vs module path
MongoDB collectionA named set of documents in MongoDB or Amazon DocumentDB. It has the same purpose as a table in a relational database. @Document("orders") names the collection that a class is stored in.A document, not a row
MongoDB documentOne stored object with its nested objects and lists inside it, such as an order with its lines. It has the same purpose as a row in a relational database. Every document has an _id.A document, not a row
MVCShort for model-view-controller. It is the pattern behind Spring MVC, which is the web framework of Spring for controllers. Spring MVC does the same as ASP.NET Core MVC.Controllers, routing and binding
N+1 problemLoading a list with one query, and then running one more query for each item to fetch the related data of that item. It is the same trap as in Entity Framework.Counting the queries in a loop
NPAPIShort for Netscape Plugin API. It is the old browser plug-in interface that Java applets needed. Browsers removed it, and that ended applets.Web frameworks, in order of extinction
NPEShort for NullPointerException. It is thrown when code uses a null reference. It does the same as NullReferenceException in C#.The gap, stated plainly
ObjectIdThe kind of id that MongoDB generates for a document. Spring Data MongoDB stores a generated String id as an ObjectId.A document, not a row
OIDCShort for OpenID Connect. It is the standard login protocol built on OAuth 2.0. It is used with identity providers such as Entra ID or Keycloak.Concept mapping
OOMShort for OutOfMemoryError. It is thrown when the JVM cannot get more memory of some kind, such as heap or metaspace. It is an Error, not an Exception.Errors, not exceptions
OpenTelemetryThe open standard for traces, metrics and logs across services. Spring Boot and .NET both support it.Tracing
OptionalA container that holds a value or nothing. It is used as a return type to say that a result may be missing. It is not a replacement for every null.Optional is for return values
ORMShort for object-relational mapper. It is a library that maps classes to database tables, such as Hibernate or Entity Framework.The landscape
@OverrideAn annotation that says that a method replaces a method from a parent class or interface. The compiler reports an error if nothing is actually overridden.Always write @Override
packageA named group of classes, such as com.acme.billing. It is like a namespace in C#, but its folders are expected to match the name, and it is also an access boundary.Packages are not namespaces
package-privateThe default access in Java when you write no modifier. A package-private class or member is visible to every class in the same package, and nowhere else.The mapping
PECSShort for producer extends, consumer super. It is the rule for wildcards. Use ? extends T for a collection you read from, and ? super T for a collection you add to.Variance is at the use site
permitsThe clause in a sealed class or interface that lists the only types allowed to extend it.Sealed types: Java's discriminated unions
persistence contextThe set of entities that one EntityManager is tracking. It is like the change tracker of a DbContext. It usually lasts as long as one transaction.Lazy loading and detached entities
pinningA virtual thread staying attached to its carrier thread while the virtual thread blocks, so the carrier thread cannot run other work. Java 24 removed the main cause, which was synchronized blocks.Pinning: the one performance trap
platform threadAn ordinary Java thread, which is backed by exactly one operating system thread. Every Java thread was a platform thread before virtual threads.The colour problem, and how Java sidestepped it
pointcutAn expression that picks which methods an aspect wraps, such as execution(public * *(..)) for every public method.AOP: writing your own cross-cutting behaviour
POJOShort for plain old Java object. It is an ordinary class with fields, getters and setters, and no framework base class.The property gap
POMShort for Project Object Model. It is the pom.xml file that describes a Maven project. It does the same as a .csproj file in .NET.pom.xml against csproj
preview featureA language or library feature that is finished but not yet final, and may still change. You must switch it on with --enable-preview to use it.What it targets
primitive streamA stream of int, long or double values. One example is IntStream. A primitive stream avoids boxing each number, and it adds methods such as sum().Primitive streams
ProblemDetailThe Spring class for an RFC 9457 error response body. It does the same as ProblemDetails in ASP.NET Core.ProblemDetail
proxyAn object that Spring puts in front of your bean. The proxy adds behaviour, such as a transaction, before it calls your method. Calls from inside the bean skip the proxy.What a proxy actually is
R2DBCShort for Reactive Relational Database Connectivity. It is a non-blocking database API for reactive applications. It is like Java Database Connectivity (JDBC), but for reactive code.When it is still the right answer
raw typeA generic type used without its type argument, such as List instead of List<String>. It exists for old code and switches off type checking.Raw types
reactiveA style in which code describes a pipeline of asynchronous events. The code uses the Mono and Flux types of Reactor. Spring WebFlux is built on this style.The model
recordA short class that holds data. Its equals, hashCode, toString and accessors are generated. A Java record is like a record in C#. Its fields cannot be reassigned.The basics
record patternA pattern that takes a record apart into its components while matching it, such as case Point(int x, int y).Record patterns
ReentrantLockA lock object that means the same as synchronized. It also has extras, such as tryLock with a timeout.ReentrantLock
relaxed bindingSpring Boot matching a setting to a property even when the name is written differently. So rates.timeout-seconds, rates.timeoutSeconds and the environment variable RATES_TIMEOUT_SECONDS all set the same value.IOptions becomes @ConfigurationProperties
release trainThe Java schedule of a new version every six months, in March and September. An LTS release comes every two years.The release train
REPLShort for read-eval-print loop. It is a prompt where you type code and see the result immediately. The REPL of Java is called JShell.jshell: run one line of Java
replica setA group of database instances that hold the same data. One instance is the primary, and it takes every write. The other instances are replicas, and they can serve reads. An Amazon DocumentDB connection string names the replica set rs0.Two parameters that change behaviour
retryable writeA write that the driver may send a second time when the first attempt fails on a network error. Drivers switch retryable writes on by default. Amazon DocumentDB supports retryable writes from engine version 8.0.2.Connecting to Amazon DocumentDB
RMIShort for Remote Method Invocation. It is the old Java way of calling methods on objects in another process, like .NET Remoting. It depends on Java serialization.Java's built-in serialization, and why to avoid it
rollback ruleThe rule for which exceptions undo a Spring transaction. By default, an unchecked exception undoes the transaction, and a checked exception does not.The rollback rule
SAMShort for single abstract method. It is the name for an interface with exactly one method to implement. You can write a lambda in place of such an interface. Such an interface is also called a functional interface.Lambdas and method references
@ScheduledA Spring annotation that runs a method on a timer or a cron schedule. It is like a hosted background service in .NET.Scheduling
ScopedValueA value that is available to a block of code and to every method that the block calls. It is also available to threads started in a structured scope. It replaces AsyncLocal-style context.ScopedValue replaces AsyncLocal
SDKMANA command-line tool that installs Java versions and switches between them.Installing and switching
sealed typeA class or interface that lists every type allowed to extend it, so a switch over it can cover every case.Sealed types: Java's discriminated unions
self-invocationA bean calling one of its own methods. The call skips the Spring proxy, so annotations such as @Transactional on that method do nothing.Self-invocation: a call from inside the class
sequenced collectionA collection with a defined order, and with methods such as getFirst() and reversed(). Sequenced collections were added in Java 21.Sequenced collections
servletThe Jakarta standard for handling an HTTP request in Java. Spring MVC runs on top of it. A servlet filter does the same as middleware in ASP.NET Core.Middleware
SLF4JShort for Simple Logging Facade for Java. It is the logging interface that Java code writes to, like ILogger in .NET. A library such as Logback does the writing.SLF4J and Logback against ILogger and Serilog
SpELShort for Spring Expression Language. It is a language for small expressions inside annotations and configuration, written #{...}.SpEL
SPIShort for service provider interface. It is an interface that a library defines for others to implement. The implementations are found at runtime from files in META-INF.Auto-configuration
Spring Data repositoryAn interface that you declare, such as OrderRepository extends JpaRepository<Order, Long>. Spring generates the data-access code for it.Repositories
Spring profileA named set of configuration, such as dev or prod, that Spring switches on at startup. It is like an environment in ASP.NET Core.Profiles are environments
starterA Spring Boot dependency that adds a group of libraries for one job. One example is spring-boot-starter-web for a web API. Boot 4 names this starter spring-boot-starter-webmvc.Starters
static importAn import that brings the static members of a class into scope, so you can write max(a, b) instead of Math.max(a, b). It is like using static in C#.Imports
STOMPShort for Simple Text Oriented Messaging Protocol. It is a simple messaging protocol that Spring runs over WebSockets for publish and subscribe.WebSockets and the SignalR gap
stream collectorThe object that turns the elements of a stream into a final result, such as a list or a map, when you call collect(). Collectors.toList() is one collector.Collectors
stream pipelineA chain of operations on a sequence, such as filter, map and collect. The chain runs once, when the final operation is called. A stream pipeline does the same as LINQ to Objects in .NET.The shape
structured concurrencyRunning related tasks in a scope that ends only when all the tasks finish. If one task fails, the scope cancels the other tasks. Structured concurrency is a preview feature in Java 25.The problem it solves
switch expressionA switch that returns a value, written with case X -> result. It is like a switch expression in C#. A Java switch expression must cover every possible case.The arrow form
synchronizedA keyword that lets only one thread at a time run a block or method for a given object. It is like the lock statement in C#.Mutual exclusion
system propertyA key and value passed to the JVM with -Dname=value, and read with System.getProperty. It is separate from environment variables.System properties and environment variables
TCKShort for Technology Compatibility Kit. It is the test suite that a JDK must pass to be called Java compatible. This is why the major distributions behave the same.Which distribution
TemurinA free, widely used JDK distribution from the Eclipse Adoptium project.Which distribution
test sliceA Spring Boot test that starts only one layer of the application, such as the controllers or the repositories, so it runs faster.Test slices
TestcontainersA library that starts real databases and message brokers in Docker containers for a test run. It exists for .NET too.Testcontainers
text blockA multi-line string written between three double quotes. It is like a raw string literal in C#.Text blocks
ThreadLocalA variable with a separate value for each thread. Scoped values are the modern way to pass context.ThreadLocal on virtual threads
transaction propagationWhat a transactional method does when a transaction is already running. The method can join the running transaction, which is the default. It can also start a new transaction, or refuse to run.Propagation
@TransactionalA Spring annotation that runs a method inside a database transaction. The transaction is committed when the method returns. It is rolled back when the method throws an unchecked exception.The default
trust storeA file of certificates that a Java program trusts when it opens an encrypted connection. The JDK tool keytool builds one.A trust store made with keytool: one of AWS's two Java routes
try-with-resourcesA try statement that opens resources in brackets after try and closes them automatically at the end. It is like the using statement in C#.try-with-resources
type erasureJava removing generic type arguments when it compiles, so at runtime a List<String> is just a List. C# keeps the type arguments.What erasure takes away
type patternA type check and a cast in one step, such as if (o instanceof String s). It is like is string s in C#.Type patterns
unchecked exceptionAn exception that the compiler does not make you catch. The unchecked exceptions are RuntimeException and its subclasses. Every C# exception behaves this way.Checked exceptions
unnamed variableThe underscore _, written in place of a variable or a pattern component that you do not need. It is like the discard in C#. It is final since Java 22.Nested patterns and unnamed variables
varA keyword that lets the compiler infer the type of a local variable from its value, exactly as in C#.var
varargsA last parameter written Type... name, which accepts any number of arguments. It is like params in C#.Varargs
virtual threadA lightweight thread that the JVM manages. You can run millions of them, so plain blocking code scales without async and await.Creating and running them
volatileA field modifier that makes every write visible to other threads immediately, and stops reordering around it. It does not make ++ safe.volatile means more in Java
WARShort for web application archive. It is a JAR-like file for deploying a web application to an application server. Spring Boot services usually run as a JAR instead.EJB and the application server
warmupThe first seconds or minutes after startup, while the just-in-time (JIT) compiler is still turning busy code into fast machine code.The JIT and warmup
when guardA condition added to a pattern with when, such as case Card c when c.last4().equals("0000"). The arm matches only if the pattern matches and the condition is true, as in C#.Pattern matching in switch
wildcardA ? in a generic type, such as List<? extends Number>. It means some unknown type. It gives Java the flexibility that C# gets from in and out.Variance is at the use site
witherA method such as withQuantity(3) that returns a copy of a record with one component changed. Java has no with expression, so you write withers yourself.The missing with expression
wrapper typeThe object version of a primitive, such as Integer for int. Collections and generics need wrappers, because they cannot hold primitives.Wrapper types
yieldThe keyword that returns a value from a block inside a switch expression. It is not related to yield return in C#.Multi-statement arms
ZGCA JVM garbage collector designed for very short pauses, even on large heaps.Choosing a collector

Appendix I: Your library, translated#

Appendices · Chapter 63· 17 min read

This chapter lists the libraries you use in .NET. For each library, it names the Java library that does the same job. Every row is indexed. So press ⌘K, or Ctrl+K, and type the .NET name to find its row.

The rows added in October 2026 were checked against each project's own documentation in that month. Not every older row was checked again then.

Some rows name several Java libraries. If Spring Boot uses one of them by default, that library comes first, and the note says when to choose another library. Some .NET libraries are copies of a Java original that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Examples are NPOI, Akka.NET and ZXing.Net. The row of such a library says so.

Web and API#

.NETJavaNote
ASP.NET CoreSpring BootSpring Boot is the usual choice. Spring led Java web frameworks with 65% in the JetBrains survey of 2025.
Minimal APIsSpring Boot, Javalin, Helidonstay with Spring Boot in a Spring team, but Javalin is closest in style, with routes written as lambdas
Kestrelembedded Tomcat, Jetty, NettyTomcat is the default in Boot. A starter replaces Tomcat with Jetty, and WebFlux applications run on Netty.
IIS hostinga JAR with an embedded serverthe JAR contains its own web server, so there is no separate server to deploy it into
Swashbuckle / NSwagspringdoc-openapiIt reads your controllers at run time and serves the OpenAPI document. Use version 3 with Boot 4.
SignalRSpring WebSocket + STOMPno direct equivalent, but WebSocket plus the STOMP protocol is closest
gRPC for .NETgrpc-java, Spring gRPCgrpc-java is the gRPC project's own library, and Spring gRPC configures grpc-java servers and clients in Spring
YARPSpring Cloud Gatewaya library for building an API gateway on Spring, and the library has a WebFlux version and a Web MVC version
OcelotSpring Cloud Gatewaythe same library replaces both YARP and Ocelot, and it does routing, rate limiting and path rewriting
Hot ChocolateSpring for GraphQLSpring's GraphQL support, built on the GraphQL Java library by both teams together
Asp.Versioningbuilt into Spring Framework 7Boot 4 selects an API version by header, path or query parameter, with no extra library
BlazorVaadin, Thymeleaf, JTEno equivalent model, but Vaadin is closest for server-driven UI
Razor / Razor PagesThymeleaf, JTE, FreemarkerBoot auto-configures Thymeleaf, FreeMarker and Mustache, and JTE provides its own Boot starter

Here is the smallest web endpoint in each framework. It is a greeting that takes a name from the path:

ASP.NET Core Minimal API
var app = WebApplication.Create(args);

app.MapGet("/hello/{name}",
    (string name) => $"hello {name}");

app.Run();
Spring Boot
@RestController
class HelloController {

    @GetMapping("/hello/{name}")
    String hello(@PathVariable String name) {
        return "hello " + name;
    }
}
Reading the code
@GetMapping("/hello/{name}")

@GetMapping maps GET /hello/{name} to this method, like MapGet in ASP.NET Core.

@PathVariable String name

@PathVariable takes name from the path. A Minimal API does the same by matching the name of the parameter.

Security and identity#

This table shows which part of Spring Security, or which separate server, replaces each .NET security library. For the code, see the chapter Security.

.NETJavaNote
ASP.NET Core authentication and authorizationSpring Securitythe standard for securing Spring applications, with login, access rules and attack protection in one framework
ASP.NET Core IdentitySpring Security with your own user tables, KeycloakNo full equivalent exists. Spring Security checks passwords, and you write registration and reset, or run Keycloak.
Duende IdentityServer / OpenIddictSpring Authorization Server, KeycloakSpring Authorization Server is a framework for your own token server, and part of Spring Security since 7.0. Keycloak is a ready-made server.
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearerSpring Security OAuth2 resource serverIt checks the bearer token on every request. Set the issuer address, and Boot configures the rest.
System.IdentityModel.Tokens.JwtNimbus JOSE + JWTthe library that Spring Security itself uses to parse tokens and check their signatures
Microsoft.Identity.WebSpring Cloud Azureits Microsoft Entra ID support signs users in with their work or school accounts
BCrypt.NetSpring Security PasswordEncoderthe default encoder hashes with bcrypt, and can move to a newer algorithm while old hashes still work

Data access#

.NETJavaNote
Entity Framework CoreHibernate / Spring Data JPABoot's JPA starter includes Hibernate, and Spring Data JPA adds repository interfaces that use Hibernate
DapperJdbcClient, JdbcTemplate, JDBIYou write the SQL, and the library maps rows to objects. Boot configures JdbcClient, so start with JdbcClient.
LINQ to SQL, IQueryablejOOQbuilds type-safe SQL in Java code, using classes it generates from your database schema
ADO.NETJDBCthe low-level database API that every Java driver implements
EF MigrationsFlyway, LiquibaseFlyway runs versioned SQL files in order. Choose Liquibase for changelogs in YAML or XML with rollbacks.
DbUpFlywaythe same idea as DbUp, with SQL scripts that each run once, in order, and are recorded as done
FluentMigratorFlyway Java migrations, LiquibaseFlyway also accepts migrations written as Java classes, and Liquibase describes changes in YAML or XML
DbContextEntityManager, or a Spring Data repositorythe unit of work that tracks the entities you loaded
IDbConnectionDataSource, Connectiona DataSource gives you pooled connections, and HikariCP is the default pool in Boot
Npgsql / SqlClientthe PostgreSQL / MSSQL JDBC drivera driver JAR on the classpath, chosen by its JDBC URL
EF Core InMemory providerH2an embedded database that Boot configures with no connection URL, once its dependency is added
StackExchange.RedisLettuce, JedisLettuce is the default in Boot's Redis starter, and Jedis is the other client that Boot can configure
MongoDB.Drivermongodb-driver-sync, Spring Data MongoDBThe official blocking driver is mongodb-driver-sync. For the repositories that Spring Data MongoDB adds, see the chapter Document data.
Elasticsearch.Netelasticsearch-java (co.elastic.clients)the official Java API Client, with typed requests and responses for every Elasticsearch API

For MongoDB, and for Amazon DocumentDB through the MongoDB API, see the chapter Document data. That chapter shows the .NET driver and Spring Data MongoDB side by side.

Here each library loads the orders of one customer with SQL that you write yourself. customerId holds the id of the customer:

Dapper
var orders = conn.Query<Order>(
    "select id, total from orders where customer_id = @Id",
    new { Id = customerId });
Spring JdbcClient
List<Order> orders = jdbcClient
    .sql("select id, total from orders where customer_id = :id")
    .param("id", customerId)
    .query(Order.class)        // columns mapped to the record's components
    .list();
Reading the code
.param("id", customerId)

This line gives a value to :id in the SQL, like the anonymous-object parameter in Dapper.

.query(Order.class)

This line maps each row to an Order. It matches the columns to the components of the record by name.

.list();

This line runs the query and returns the rows as a List<Order>.

Mapping and validation#

This table covers two jobs. The first job is copying one object into another, which AutoMapper does. The second job is checking input, which FluentValidation does.

.NETJavaNote
AutoMapper, MapsterMapStruct, ModelMapperMapStruct generates the mapping code when you compile, but ModelMapper matches properties by convention instead
FluentValidation rulesJakarta Validation with Hibernate ValidatorRules are annotations on the fields, not a separate validator class. Boot's validation starter includes both libraries.
DataAnnotations attributesJakarta Validation annotations@NotNull and @Size are the same idea as [Required] and [StringLength], and they are checked where a parameter has @Valid

For MapStruct in code, see the section MapStruct against AutoMapper. For validation, see the chapter Validation and error responses.

Serialisation#

.NETJavaNote
System.Text.JsonJacksonthe default in Spring Boot, which configures it for you
Newtonsoft.JsonJackson, GsonJackson is the default JSON library in Boot, and Boot also configures Gson when Gson is on the classpath
JsonSerializer.SerializeobjectMapper.writeValueAsStringturns an object into a JSON String, the same job as Serialize
[JsonPropertyName]@JsonPropertysets the JSON name of one field or record component
[JsonIgnore]@JsonIgnoreleaves one field or record component out of the JSON
JsonSerializerOptionsObjectMapper configurationthe options are set once on the mapper, and Spring Boot builds the mapper from properties
protobuf-netprotobuf-javaprotobuf-java uses code generated from .proto files, but protobuf-net uses attributes
MessagePackmsgpack-javamsgpack-java is the MessagePack project's Java library, and its Jackson module maps objects through Jackson
YamlDotNetSnakeYAML, Jackson YAMLSpring Boot reads application.yaml with SnakeYAML, and Jackson YAML maps YAML to your classes
CsvHelperOpenCSV, Apache Commons CSV, Jackson CSVOpenCSV binds rows to annotated classes, and Commons CSV and Jackson CSV also read and write CSV files
Gotcha

Spring Boot 4 moves to Jackson 3. The root package of Jackson 3 is tools.jackson, not com.fasterxml.jackson. So every Jackson import changes, except the imports of annotations. The annotations stay in com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.

Boot renamed several of its own types at the same time. @JsonComponent became @JacksonComponent. @JsonMixin became @JacksonMixin. See Migrating Boot 3 to 4.

DI, logging, config#

.NETJavaNote
Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjectionSpring, or Jakarta CDIthe container is part of the framework, not a separate package
AutofacSpringinside a Spring application you use Spring's container, so there is no second container library to choose
ScrutorSpring component scanningscanning is built in, so Spring finds classes marked @Component, @Service or @Repository by itself
ILogger<T>SLF4J Loggerthe interface that your code calls, and Logback implements this interface
SerilogLogback, Log4j2Spring Boot logs through Logback unless you switch to another library
NLogLogback, Log4j2Logback is the default in Boot, and Boot also includes a default configuration for Log4j2 if you switch
structured loggingLogstash encoder, or Boot structured loggingstructured logging means JSON log lines, and Spring Boot 3.4 and later writes them with no extra library
IConfigurationSpring Environmentone object answers every property lookup, whichever file or variable the value came from
appsettings.jsonapplication.yml / application.propertiesBoot loads either file by itself at startup, and the YAML form nests keys as appsettings.json does
IOptions<T>@ConfigurationPropertiesbinds a configuration section to a typed class or record
User Secretsa local profile, or Vaultkeep secrets out of the repository, in an ignored local file or in Vault
Azure App ConfigurationSpring Cloud Azure, Spring Cloud ConfigSpring Cloud Azure reads App Configuration itself, but Spring Cloud Config serves settings from Git instead
Microsoft.FeatureManagementTogglz, OpenFeatureTogglz has a Spring Boot starter, and OpenFeature is a vendor-neutral API that also has a .NET SDK

Caching#

A Spring application rarely calls a cache directly. It marks a method with @Cacheable and chooses a store. So this table maps each .NET cache to a store. For the code, see the chapter Caching, scheduling and events.

.NETJavaNote
IMemoryCacheCaffeinean in-process cache with size and time limits, which Boot can put behind @Cacheable
IDistributedCache with RedisSpring Data Redisits RedisCacheManager keeps the same @Cacheable entries in Redis, shared by every instance
HybridCacheno direct equivalentBoot's cache providers include no two-level cache, so you combine Caffeine and Redis in your own code

Resilience, messaging, scheduling#

.NETJavaNote
PollyResilience4jthe choice for Boot 3, and it is a separate library
PollySpring Framework @Retryablethe choice for Boot 4, because retry moved into the framework
HttpClientFactoryRestClient, HTTP interface clientsRestClient is the modern client, and Boot configures its builder for you
Refit@HttpExchange interfacesdeclare an interface, and Spring generates the HTTP client
RestSharp, FlurlRestClientSpring's RestClient is already a fluent HTTP client, so the same style needs no extra library
MediatRSpring ApplicationEvents, Axonno single library does everything that MediatR does
MassTransit / NServiceBusSpring Cloud Stream, Spring Integration, Camel, AxonNo single library matches. Spring Cloud Stream hides the broker, and Spring Integration and Camel route messages.
RabbitMQ.ClientSpring AMQPuse RabbitTemplate to send and @RabbitListener to receive
Confluent.KafkaSpring Kafkause KafkaTemplate to send and @KafkaListener to receive
HangfireQuartz, JobRunr, Spring @Scheduled@Scheduled is good for simple timers. Quartz and JobRunr can keep jobs in a database, and JobRunr has a dashboard.
Quartz.NETQuartzQuartz is the Java scheduler of the same name. Boot has a starter for it and can keep its jobs in your database.
Azure FunctionsSpring Cloud Functionyou write the logic as a plain function, and adapters run it on Azure Functions, AWS Lambda or Google Cloud
System.ReactiveProject Reactor, RxJavaSpring WebFlux is built on Reactor, and RxJava is the Reactive Extensions library for the JVM
Akka.NETAkka, Apache PekkoAkka.NET is a port of Akka, and Pekko is a fork of Akka 2.6 that stayed under the Apache licence
OrleansApache Pekko, Akkathe nearest match is cluster sharding, which reaches an actor by a logical id on any node

Documents and files#

This table covers the files and messages that a business application handles. They are spreadsheets, PDF documents, HTML pages, images, barcodes and email.

.NETJavaNote
ClosedXML, EPPlusApache POIreads and writes Excel files, both .xlsx and .xls, and also Word and PowerPoint files
NPOIApache POIApache POI is the original, and NPOI describes itself as the .NET version of Apache POI
QuestPDFOpenPDF, Apache PDFBoxOpenPDF creates PDFs and can render them from HTML, and PDFBox also extracts text and fills forms
iText for .NETiTextthe same product for Java, with the same choice between the AGPL and a commercial licence
HtmlAgilityPack, AngleSharpjsoupparses real-world HTML into a tree that you query with CSS selectors or XPath
ImageSharpImageIO, Thumbnailator, TwelveMonkeysImageIO is in the JDK. Thumbnailator makes thumbnails, and TwelveMonkeys adds formats such as WebP.
MailKitJakarta Mail through JavaMailSenderBoot's mail starter builds a JavaMailSender once spring.mail.host is set, and JavaMailSender uses Jakarta Mail
ZXing.NetZXingZXing is the original Java barcode library, and ZXing.Net is a port of it. ZXing is now in maintenance mode.

Cloud SDKs#

AWS and Azure each publish a Java SDK and a .NET SDK. For each Java SDK, a Spring Cloud project wraps the SDK in Spring's own style.

.NETJavaNote
AWS SDK for .NETAWS SDK for Java 2.x, Spring Cloud AWSThe SDK is from Amazon itself. Spring Cloud AWS is a community project that adds Spring-style S3 and SQS support.
Azure SDK for .NETAzure SDK for Java, Spring Cloud Azurethe client libraries are in the com.azure group, and Spring Cloud Azure adds Spring support for Service Bus and Key Vault

Testing and quality#

.NETJavaNote
xUnit / NUnitJUnit 5 (JUnit 6 on Boot 4)Boot's test starter includes JUnit, so a project does not choose a test framework
Moq / NSubstituteMockitothe mocking library in Boot's test starter, so it is already on the test classpath

ArchUnitNETArchUnitArchUnit is the original, and ArchUnitNET calls itself the C# fork of this library

Observability and diagnostics#

.NETJavaNote
dotnet-countersJFR, MicrometerJFR records JVM events, and Micrometer exposes application metrics
dotnet-trace / PerfViewJFR + JDK Mission ControlJFR records inside the JVM, and Mission Control opens the recording
dotnet-dumpjmap, jcmdheap and thread dumps taken from a running JVM
OpenTelemetry .NETOpenTelemetry Java agentan agent added at startup instruments common libraries with no change to your code
App Insights / PrometheusMicrometer + PrometheusMicrometer is the metrics interface, and a backend such as Prometheus connects to it
HealthChecksSpring Boot Actuatorhealth, metrics and info endpoints, switched on by one starter
Visual Studio Profilerasync-profiler, JMCasync-profiler draws CPU and allocation flame graphs with low overhead

Here are three commands against a running JVM whose process id is 4242:

jcmd 4242 JFR.start duration=60s filename=app.jfr   # record a running JVM for a minute
jcmd 4242 Thread.print                              # a thread dump
jmap -histo 4242 | head                             # which classes take the most heap
Reading the code
jcmd 4242 JFR.start duration=60s filename=app.jfr

This command starts a one-minute flight recording and writes it to app.jfr. The application does not restart.

jcmd 4242 Thread.print

This command prints what every thread is doing, like a thread dump from dotnet-dump.

jmap -histo 4242 | head

This command counts the objects of each class on the heap. The class that uses the most memory comes first.

Note

JFR, Java Flight Recorder, is worth learning early. JFR is a production-grade profiler that can stay switched on. It is built into the Java Development Kit (JDK). The nearest .NET tools are dotnet-trace and dotnet-counters, but they are separate tools that you install. Run jcmd <pid> JFR.start on a running process to get allocation, lock contention, I/O and CPU data with no restart. See The JVM at runtime.

Utility libraries#

.NETJavaNote
LINQStreamsStreams are built into the JDK. See the chapter Streams vs LINQ.
Humanizerno direct equivalentthere is no popular equivalent, so format such text yourself
AutoMapperMapStructMapStruct works at compile time, so mapping problems appear in the build
FluentValidationJakarta Bean Validationrules are annotations such as @NotNull and @Size, or custom validators
System.Collections.ImmutableList.of, Guava immutablesList.of and Map.of are built in, and Guava adds richer immutable types
Nito.AsyncExvirtual threadsthe problems that Nito.AsyncEx solves largely disappear with virtual threads
CommandLineParserpicocliannotation-driven command-line parsing, with generated help
Scriban / HandlebarsThymeleaf, MustacheThymeleaf and Mustache are text template libraries, and Mustache is the closest to Handlebars
NodaTimejava.timejava.time is built into the JDK, and NodaTime and java.time both descend from Joda-Time
Guard clauses librariesObjects.requireNonNull, Guava Preconditionsargument checks that throw with a clear message
OneOfsealed interfaces and recordsSealed interfaces and records are built into Java 21. A sealed interface lists its cases, and a switch must handle every case.
ErrorOra sealed Result type, or Vavrthe JDK has Optional but no Result type, so write a small sealed interface or use Either from Vavr

Statelessstateless4jThe library stateless4j is a Java port of Stateless. Spring Statemachine was archived in July 2026, so avoid it in new code.

Only in Java#

These tools are in daily use in Java teams. Most of these tools exist because Java or the JDK lacks something that C# or the .NET SDK has. The last column says what .NET does instead.

Java toolWhat it isThe problem it solvesWhat .NET does instead
LombokAnnotations that add getters, constructors and builders while the code compiles.A Java class otherwise needs every accessor and constructor written by hand.Properties, records and primary constructors are part of C#.
Annotation processors (MapStruct, Immutables)Code generators that the Java compiler runs during the build.Mapping code and value classes are repetitive to write by hand.Roslyn source generators do the same job.
jOOQA library that generates Java classes from your database and builds SQL with them.Java has no LINQ, so SQL written as text is checked only when it runs.LINQ with Entity Framework Core checks a query when you compile.
Spring Data derived queriesA repository method whose name is the query, such as findByEmailAndStatus.A simple query needs no hand-written JPQL or SQL.A LINQ Where call on a DbSet says the same thing.
GuavaGoogle's core libraries, with immutable collections, multimaps, hashing and more.The JDK's collections have no multimap or multiset.System.Collections.Immutable and ToLookup cover the common cases.
Apache CommonsSmall helper libraries such as Commons Lang, Commons IO and Commons Text.The JDK leaves out many small helpers for strings, files and collections.Most such helpers are in the base class library.
Project ReactorA library of non-blocking pipelines, built from the types Mono and Flux.A server can handle many requests with a small number of threads.async and await do this in C#, and virtual threads now do it in Java too.
Java agentsA JAR named with -javaagent, which the JVM loads before main and which can rewrite classes as they load.Tracing and profiling are added without a change to the application's code.The CLR profiler and startup hooks, both set through environment variables.
JDK Flight RecorderAn event recorder that is part of the JDK and is started with jcmd or a flag.You see what the application, the JVM and the operating system are doing.dotnet-trace and dotnet-counters, which are installed as separate tools.
SDKMANA command-line tool that installs several JDKs side by side and switches between them.Java has many JDK vendors and versions, and a project needs one of them..NET SDKs install side by side, and global.json selects one.
Maven and Gradle wrappersThe scripts mvnw and gradlew, committed with the project.They download the declared version of the build tool, so nobody installs it by hand.The dotnet command is part of the SDK, so there is nothing to download.
JBangA tool that runs one .java file and reads its dependencies from //DEPS comments.A script with dependencies otherwise needs a whole Maven or Gradle project..NET 10 runs one file with dotnet run app.cs and #:package lines.
OpenRewriteRecipes that rewrite source code automatically.Framework migrations and other mechanical changes are applied across a whole codebase.Roslyn analyzers with code fixes, which an IDE applies across a solution.
Error Prone and NullAwayPlugins for the Java compiler that report likely bugs and null errors.Java has no nullable reference types, so javac does not check for null by itself.Nullable reference types and Roslyn analyzers come with the .NET SDK.
Spring ModulithA toolkit that verifies the module structure inside one Spring Boot application.A public class is visible to every package, so module boundaries are not enforced.Separate projects and the internal keyword enforce the same boundary.
Kotlin, Scala and GroovyOther languages that run on the JVM and use the same Java libraries.A team gets a different syntax without leaving Java's libraries, and Gradle scripts use Groovy or Kotlin.F# and Visual Basic share the CLR with C# in the same way.

For Lombok in code, see the section Lombok against source generators. For MapStruct in code, see the section MapStruct against AutoMapper. Other chapters teach four more of these tools. The four tools are derived queries, Reactor, Flight Recorder and the wrappers.

Jackson against System.Text.Json#

Jackson is the most-used library in Java after the JDK itself. Spring Boot configures Jackson for you, so most of the time you only see its annotations. When you do build a mapper yourself, the options translate like this:

System.Text.Json
var opts = new JsonSerializerOptions {
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
    DefaultIgnoreCondition =
        JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull
};

string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(order, opts);
var back = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Order>(json, opts);
Jackson 3 (Boot 4)
JsonMapper mapper = JsonMapper.builder()     // tools.jackson.databind.json
    .changeDefaultPropertyInclusion(
        incl -> incl.withValueInclusion(Include.NON_NULL))
    .build();                                // java.time works with no module

String json = mapper.writeValueAsString(order);
Order back = mapper.readValue(json, Order.class);
Reading the code
JsonMapper mapper = JsonMapper.builder()

Jackson 3 builds its mapper once, with a builder. C# fills in an options object instead.

incl -> incl.withValueInclusion(Include.NON_NULL)

This setting leaves null values out of the JSON, like WhenWritingNull in C#.

mapper.readValue(json, Order.class)

This call passes the class, because erasure removes the type argument. See Generics and type erasure.

C# refresherNewtonsoft.Json: JsonConvertC# 3
string json = JsonConvert.SerializeObject(order);
var back = JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<Order>(json);
Note

On Boot 3, with Jackson 2, the same code differs in three ways:

  • It imports from com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.
  • It needs .addModule(new JavaTimeModule()) for java.time types.
  • It usually leaves null values out with .serializationInclusion(Include.NON_NULL).

The annotations below are the same in both versions.

Settings for single fields are attributes in C#, and annotations in Java. Here an order renames its id, hides a secret, and formats its total with a custom serializer:

Attributes
public record Order(
    [property: JsonPropertyName("order_id")] long Id,
    [property: JsonIgnore] string Secret,
    [property: JsonConverter(typeof(MoneyConverter))]
    decimal Total);
Annotations
public record Order(
    @JsonProperty("order_id") long id,
    @JsonIgnore String secret,
    @JsonSerialize(using = MoneySerializer.class)
    BigDecimal total) { }
Reading the code
@JsonProperty("order_id") long id

This annotation writes the component as order_id, like JsonPropertyName in C#.

@JsonIgnore String secret

This annotation leaves the component out of the JSON entirely.

@JsonSerialize(using = MoneySerializer.class)

This annotation names a custom serializer, like a JsonConverter in C#. MoneySerializer is your own class.

System.Text.JsonJacksonNote
JsonSerializer.Serializemapper.writeValueAsStringreturns the JSON as a String, as Serialize does
JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>mapper.readValue(s, T.class)pass the class, because erasure removes the type argument
Deserialize a generic typenew TypeReference<List<T>>() { }the trailing braces make a subclass that keeps List<T> at run time
[JsonPropertyName]@JsonPropertywrites and reads the member under the JSON name you give
[JsonIgnore]@JsonIgnoreleaves the member out of the JSON entirely
[JsonConverter]@JsonSerialize / @JsonDeserializenames your own serializer or deserializer class for one member
JsonSerializerOptionsJsonMapper.builder()Jackson 3 sets options on a builder, then builds the mapper once
CamelCase policyPropertyNamingStrategies.LOWER_CAMEL_CASErarely needed, because Java field names are already camelCase
DateTime supportbuilt in (Jackson 3), JavaTimeModule (Jackson 2)Jackson 3 handles java.time itself, but Jackson 2 needs the module
Unknown members ignoredFAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIESJackson 2 fails on unknown members by default, but Jackson 3 ignores them
Gotcha

Two Jackson defaults changed between Boot 3 and Boot 4. Boot 3 uses Jackson 2. Jackson 2 throws on an unknown JSON property unless you disable FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES. Jackson 2 also writes java.time types as unreadable objects unless JavaTimeModule is registered.

Boot 4 uses Jackson 3. Jackson 3 ignores unknown properties and handles java.time itself, as System.Text.Json does. On Boot 3 and on Boot 4, Spring Boot configures the mapper that it builds to ignore unknown properties. So this difference affects you only when you build a mapper yourself.

MapStruct against AutoMapper#

The difference is when the mapping is decided. AutoMapper matches properties by reflection while the program runs. MapStruct writes a plain Java class when you compile. So mapping problems appear in the build, and not in production. Here an order is mapped to a data transfer object that flattens the customer's name:

AutoMapper
public class OrderProfile : Profile
{
    public OrderProfile()
    {
        CreateMap<Order, OrderDto>()
            .ForMember(d => d.CustomerName,
                o => o.MapFrom(s => s.Customer.Name));
    }
}

var dto = _mapper.Map<OrderDto>(order);
MapStruct
@Mapper(componentModel = "spring")
public interface OrderMapper {

    @Mapping(target = "customerName",
             source = "customer.name")
    OrderDto toDto(Order order);
}

// injected like any bean
var dto = orderMapper.toDto(order);
Reading the code
source = "customer.name")

This line fills customerName from the name of the order's customer, like MapFrom in AutoMapper. A field with the same name on both sides needs no line at all.

OrderDto toDto(Order order);

This is a method with no body. MapStruct writes the body when you compile.

Note

componentModel = "spring" makes the generated implementation a Spring bean, so you inject the interface and never see the generated class. To read the generated class, look in target/generated-sources. The class is ordinary field-by-field assignment. It uses no reflection and does no work at startup.

Java's built-in serialization, and why to avoid it#

Java has its own binary serialization mechanism. It is older than the popularity of JSON, and it is built into the language through the marker interface Serializable. You will see this mechanism, and you should not choose it. Here an order is written to a file, and p is the path of the file:

class Order implements Serializable {          // a marker: no methods
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
    private transient String secret;           // excluded from the bytes
}

try (var out = new ObjectOutputStream(Files.newOutputStream(p))) {
    out.writeObject(order);                    // opaque binary
}
Reading the code
class Order implements Serializable {

Serializable has no methods. It only marks that objects of the class may be serialized.

private transient String secret;

transient leaves a field out of the bytes.

out.writeObject(order);

This line writes the whole object, and every object that it refers to, in Java's own binary format.

Gotcha

Deserializing untrusted data is remote code execution. The format says which classes to create, and the reader creates them before you can inspect anything. A chain of ordinary library classes can turn a byte array into arbitrary code. Such a chain is called a gadget chain. This is the most exploited kind of Java vulnerability. It is the reason that so many Java security advisories look alike.

If you must read serialized data that you do not control, use a deserialization filter. Java 9 added deserialization filters, as JDK Enhancement Proposal (JEP) 290. A filter lists the classes that are allowed to appear:

java -Djdk.serialFilter='com.acme.**;java.base/*;!*' -jar app.jar
Reading the code
-Djdk.serialFilter='com.acme.**;java.base/*;!*'

This filter allows classes under com.acme and classes in the java.base module. It rejects every other class, before any object is built.

ProblemDetail
Securityuntrusted input can execute code, as the warning above explains
VersioningserialVersionUID must be managed by hand, or old data stops loading
Couplingthe wire format is your private field layout, so refactoring breaks it
Portabilityonly Java can read the format, and no other platform understands it
Bypasses constructorsobjects are reconstructed without running your invariants
Note

Use Jackson. You can inspect JSON and version it, and every language can read it. Reading JSON also does not create arbitrary classes. If you really need a compact binary format, use Protobuf, Avro or CBOR. All three formats have schemas, and all three formats are free of this danger.

Serializable is still required in a few places. Two examples are session objects in some servlet containers, and older code that uses Remote Method Invocation (RMI) or Jakarta Messaging (JMS). Implementing the interface is harmless. Calling readObject on bytes from outside your system is not harmless.

SLF4J and Logback against ILogger and Serilog#

The Simple Logging Facade for Java (SLF4J) is the interface, and Logback is the implementation. Your code always calls SLF4J, exactly as your C# code calls ILogger<T> and not Serilog. Here the order service logs a placed order. It also logs a warning that is tagged with a correlation id, cid:

ILogger + Serilog
private readonly ILogger<OrderService> _log;

_log.LogInformation(
    "Placed {OrderId} for {Total}", id, total);

using (_log.BeginScope(new Dictionary<string, object>
       { ["CorrelationId"] = cid }))
{
    _log.LogWarning("slow");
}
SLF4J + Logback
private static final Logger log =
    LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderService.class);

log.info("Placed {} for {}", id, total);

MDC.put("correlationId", cid);
try {
    log.warn("slow");
} finally {
    MDC.remove("correlationId");
}
Reading the code
LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderService.class)

This call gets a logger that is named after the class, like ILogger<OrderService> in C#. The field is static, so one logger serves every instance.

log.info("Placed {} for {}", id, total);

The placeholders are {}, and the arguments fill them in order. The placeholders have no names.

MDC.put("correlationId", cid);

This line adds a value to the mapped diagnostic context (MDC). Every log line on this thread then includes the value, until the value is removed. This is like BeginScope in C#.

Gotcha

SLF4J placeholders are positional {}, not named. There is no {OrderId}, so structured logging needs the MDC or a structured encoder. Here SLF4J is clearly weaker than Serilog. This is the reason that the MDC matters more in Java than logging scopes matter in .NET.

Log levels and the line format are set in application.yml. This file does most of what a Serilog configuration file does:

# application.yml covers most of what a Serilog config file would
logging:
  level:
    root: INFO
    com.acme.billing: DEBUG
  pattern:
    console: "%d{HH:mm:ss} %-5level [%X{correlationId}] %logger{36} - %msg%n"
Reading the code
com.acme.billing: DEBUG

This line logs everything from DEBUG up for the billing code. All other code stays at INFO.

[%X{correlationId}]

%X reads a value from the MDC, so each line shows its correlation id.

Lombok against source generators#

Lombok writes boilerplate code while the code compiles, and annotations tell Lombok what to write. In C#, the language itself makes most of that code unnecessary. Here is the C#, and the Lombok version:

C#
// records and primary constructors cover most of it
public record Customer(string Name, int Age);

public class Order(IOrderRepo repo)
{
    private readonly IOrderRepo _repo = repo;
}
Java 25
@Getter @Setter
@NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor
@Builder
@EqualsAndHashCode
public class Customer {
    private String name;
    private int age;
}

@RequiredArgsConstructor        // one ctor for all final fields
public class OrderService {
    private final OrderRepo repo;
}
Reading the code
@Getter @Setter

These annotations generate a getter and a setter for every field.

@RequiredArgsConstructor

This annotation generates a constructor that takes every final field. Spring passes dependencies through such a constructor.

Note

For immutable data, a record is now better than Lombok and needs no dependency. Lombok is still useful for mutable Jakarta Persistence (JPA) entities, which cannot be records. Lombok is also still useful for @Slf4j, which declares the logger field for you. @Builder is the other Lombok annotation that is still common.
